sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第227卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 227
translations.idiomatic: Volume 227 of the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance

sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十三】起重光作噩六月，盡玄黓閹茂，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records, 43] From the sixth month of the year Chongguang-Zuoe through Xuanque-Yanmao, altogether a year and a fraction more.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, 43] Covering from the sixth month of Chongguang-Zuoe through Xuanque-Yanmao—a little more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝二建中二年（

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jianzhong era of Emperor Dezong, the Sagacious, Martial, and Sagely Text Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong under Emperor Dezong, the Sagacious Martial and Literarily Accomplished Emperor (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元七八一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, corresponding to the year 781 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the xinyou year, equivalent to 781 CE)

sentences.zh: 六月，庚寅，以浙江東、西觀察使、蘇州刺史韓滉為潤州刺史、浙江東、西節度使，名其軍曰鎮海。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengyin, Han Huang, the observer of eastern and western Zhejiang and prefect of Suzhou, was appointed prefect of Runzhou and military commissioner of eastern and western Zhejiang; his army was named Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the gengyin day, Han Huang—observer of eastern and western Zhejiang and prefect of Suzhou—was made prefect of Runzhou and military commissioner for both Zhejiang circuits, and his command was titled the Zhenhai Army.

sentences.zh: 張著至襄陽，梁崇義益懼，陳兵而見之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhu arrived at Xiangyang, Liang Chongyi grew all the more fearful; he arrayed troops and received him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhu reached Xiangyang, Liang Chongyi became still more afraid; he drew up his troops and went out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 藺杲得詔不敢發，馳見崇義，請命。

translations.literal: Lin Gao received the edict but dared not promulgate it; he galloped to see Chongyi and asked for orders.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Gao had received the edict but did not dare issue it; he rode in haste to Chongyi to seek instructions.

sentences.zh: 崇義對著號泣，竟不受詔。

translations.literal: Chongyi wept aloud before Zhu and in the end would not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi wept before Zhu and ultimately refused to accept the edict.

sentences.zh: 著覆命。

translations.literal: Zhu returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu returned to make his report.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，進李希烈爵南平郡王，加漢南、漢北兵馬招討使，督諸道兵討之。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Li Xilie was advanced to Prince of Nanping Commandery and made commander for the pacification of Han South and Han North, to supervise the armies of all circuits in attacking Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day, Li Xilie was promoted to Prince of Nanping and appointed pacification commissioner for Han South and Han North, with authority to direct the forces of every circuit against Liang Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 楊炎諫曰：「希烈為董秦養子，親任無比，卒逐秦而奪其位。

translations.literal: Yang Yan remonstrated, saying: "Xilie was the adopted son of Dong Qin and enjoyed trust beyond compare; in the end he drove Qin out and seized his position.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan urged against it, saying, "Li Xilie was Dong Qin's adopted son and enjoyed unparalleled favor; in the end he expelled Qin and usurped his post.

sentences.zh: 為人狼戾無親，無功猶屈強不法，使平崇義，何以制之！」

translations.literal: By nature he is fierce and devoid of kinship ties; though he has no merit he still bends others by force and defies the law—if we send him to pacify Chongyi, how shall we control him afterward!"
translations.idiomatic: He is by nature brutal and without loyalty; though he has won no merit he already bullies others and flouts the law—if we set him to crush Chongyi, how will we restrain him afterward!"

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 炎固爭之，上益不平。

translations.literal: Yan pressed his argument firmly, and the emperor grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued all the more insistently, and the emperor's resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 荊南牙門將吳少誠以取梁崇義之策干李希烈，希烈以少誠為前鋒。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng, a gate officer of Jingnan, presented Li Xilie with a plan to take Liang Chongyi; Xilie made Shaocheng his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng, a staff officer of Jingnan, offered Li Xilie a plan to capture Liang Chongyi, and Xilie appointed him vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 少誠，幽州潞人也。

translations.literal: Shaocheng was a native of Lu in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng was a man of Lu in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 時內自關中，西暨蜀、漢，南盡江、淮、閩、越，北至太原，所在出兵，而李正己遣兵扼徐州甬橋、渦口，梁崇義阻兵襄陽，運路皆絕，人心震恐。

translations.literal: At that time, within the realm from Guanzhong in the west through Shu and Han, south to the Yangtze, Huai, Min, and Yue, and north to Taiyuan, troops were raised everywhere; yet Li Zhengji sent soldiers to hold Yongqiao at Xuzhou and Wokou, while Liang Chongyi blocked the roads at Xiangyang, so all supply routes were cut and hearts everywhere shook with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the empire—from Guanzhong westward through Shu and Han, south to the Yangtze, Huai, Min, and Yue regions, and north to Taiyuan—armies were mobilized on every side; yet Li Zhengji held Yongqiao near Xuzhou and Wokou with his troops, and Liang Chongyi blocked the routes at Xiangyang, severing all transport lines and spreading panic among the people.

sentences.zh: 江、淮進奉船千餘艘，泊渦口不敢進。

translations.literal: More than a thousand tribute ships from the Jiang and Huai regions lay at anchor at Wokou and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand tribute vessels from the Jiang and Huai circuits lay moored at Wokou, afraid to proceed.

sentences.zh: 上以和州刺史張萬福為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Zhang Wanfu, prefect of Hezhou, prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Zhang Wanfu, prefect of Hezhou, to be prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 萬福馳至渦口，立馬岸上，發進奉船，淄青將士停岸睥睨不敢動。

translations.literal: Wanfu galloped to Wokou, stood his horse on the bank, and ordered the tribute ships to sail; the officers and soldiers of Ziqing stood on the shore glaring but did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu rode at full speed to Wokou, reined up on the bank, and sent the tribute fleet on its way; the Ziqing troops on shore glared but did not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，汾陽忠武王郭子儀薨。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Guo Ziyi, Prince of Zhongwu of Fenyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, Guo Ziyi, the Loyal and Martial Prince of Fenyang, passed away.

sentences.zh: 子儀為上將，擁強兵，程元振、魚朝恩讒謗百端；

translations.literal: Ziyi was the empire's foremost general and held a powerful army; Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en slandered him in every way;
translations.idiomatic: As the empire's preeminent commander with a formidable army at his back, Guo Ziyi was slandered from every quarter by Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en;

sentences.zh: 詔書一紙徵之，無不即日就道，由是讒謗不行。

translations.literal: yet at a single sheet of imperial summons he would always set out the same day, and so the slanders could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: yet whenever a single edict summoned him, he would set out that very day—so the calumny never took hold.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣使至田承嗣所，承嗣西望拜之曰：「此膝不屈於人若干年矣！」

translations.literal: Once he sent an envoy to Tian Chengsi; Chengsi bowed toward the west and said, "These knees have not bent before another man for many years!"
translations.idiomatic: He once sent an envoy to Tian Chengsi, who bowed toward the west and said, "These knees have not bowed to any man for many years!"

sentences.zh: 李靈曜據汴州作亂，公私物過汴者皆留之，惟子儀物不敢近，遣兵衛送出境。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao seized Bianzhou in rebellion, all public and private goods passing through Bian were detained—only Ziyi's goods no one dared touch; troops were sent to escort them beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao held Bianzhou in revolt, every public and private shipment passing through was seized—only Guo Ziyi's property no one dared approach; soldiers were dispatched to guard it safely out of the region.

sentences.zh: 校中書令考凡二十四，月入俸錢二萬緡，私產不在焉；

translations.literal: He was assessed as Grand Counselor twenty-four times; his monthly salary was twenty thousand strings of cash, not counting his private estates;
translations.idiomatic: He had been rated as Grand Counselor on twenty-four occasions; his monthly stipend was twenty thousand strings of cash, apart from his private holdings;

sentences.zh: 府庫珍貨山積。

translations.literal: his treasuries piled precious goods like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: and his storehouses overflowed with treasure.

sentences.zh: 家人三千人，八子、七婿皆為朝廷顯官；

translations.literal: his household numbered three thousand persons; his eight sons and seven sons-in-law all held eminent posts at court;
translations.idiomatic: His household numbered three thousand souls; his eight sons and seven sons-in-law all held high office at court;

sentences.zh: 諸孫數十人，每問安，不能盡辯，頷之而已。

translations.literal: his grandsons numbered several dozen—when they came to pay their respects he could not recognize them all and would only nod.
translations.idiomatic: he had dozens of grandsons; when they came to greet him he could not tell them apart and would merely nod in reply.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩、李懷光、渾瑊輩皆出麾下，雖貴為王公，常頤指役使，趨走於前，家人亦以僕隸視之。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en, Li Huaiguang, Hun Jian, and the like had all risen under his command; though ennobled as princes and dukes, he would often order them about with a gesture of his chin and they would hurry before him—his own household treated them as servants too.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en, Li Huaiguang, Hun Jian, and others had all served under him; though raised to princely rank, he would snap his chin to command them and they would run to obey—his own family regarded them as household servants.

sentences.zh: 天下以其身為安危者殆三十年，功蓋天下而主不疑，位極人臣而眾不疾，窮奢極欲而人不非之，年八十五而終。

translations.literal: For nearly thirty years the realm looked to his person for safety or peril; his merit covered the world yet the sovereign never doubted him, his rank reached the summit among subjects yet none resented him, his luxury and indulgence reached extremes yet men did not reproach him—and he died at eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly thirty years the empire's fate seemed bound to his person; his achievements overshadowed the realm yet the throne never mistrusted him, he stood at the pinnacle of subjecthood yet aroused no envy, he lived in the utmost extravagance yet drew no blame—and he died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 其將佐至大官、為名臣者甚眾。

translations.literal: Among his subordinates, many rose to high office and became renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his lieutenants rose to high rank and became celebrated statesmen.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以懷、鄭、河陽節度副使李艽為河陽、懷州節度使，割東畿五縣隸焉。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Li Wan, vice commissioner of the Huai, Zheng, and Heyang circuits, was made military commissioner of Heyang and Huaizhou; five counties of the eastern capital district were detached and placed under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day, Li Wan, deputy commissioner of the Huai, Zheng, and Heyang circuits, was appointed military commissioner of Heyang and Huaizhou, with five eastern capital counties assigned to his command.

sentences.zh: 北庭、安西自吐蕃陷河、隴，隔絕不通，伊西、北庭節度使李元忠、四鎮留後郭昕帥將士閉境拒守，數遣使奉表，皆不達，聲問絕者十餘年。

translations.literal: Beiting and Anxi had been cut off since the Tibetans took He and Long; Li Yuanzhong, military commissioner of Yixi and Beiting, and Guo Xin, acting commissioner of the Four Garrisons, led their troops in closing the borders and holding out, repeatedly sending envoys with memorials that never arrived—no word had been heard for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tibetans had overrun He and Long, Beiting and Anxi had been severed from the empire; Li Yuanzhong, commissioner of Yixi and Beiting, and Guo Xin, acting commissioner of the Four Garrisons, held their frontiers shut and defended them, sending memorial after memorial that never reached the court—for more than ten years no news came through.

sentences.zh: 至是，遣使間道歷諸胡自回紇中來，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Now they sent envoys by secret routes through the various barbarians, coming out from among the Uyghurs; the emperor praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At last they dispatched envoys by hidden paths through the frontier peoples, emerging from Uyghur territory; the emperor commended them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊午朔，加元忠北庭大都護，賜爵寧塞郡王；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day wuwu, Yuanzhong was made Grand Protector of Beiting and enfeoffed as Prince of Ningsai Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month (wuwu), Yuanzhong was promoted to Grand Protector of Beiting and created Prince of Ningsai;

sentences.zh: 以昕為安西大都護、四鎮節度使，賜爵武威郡王；

translations.literal: Xin was made Grand Protector of Anxi and military commissioner of the Four Garrisons, enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xin was appointed Grand Protector of Anxi and military commissioner of the Four Garrisons, and created Prince of Wuwei;

sentences.zh: 將士皆遷七資。

translations.literal: officers and soldiers alike were advanced seven grades in rank.
translations.idiomatic: and all officers and soldiers were promoted seven steps in rank.

sentences.zh: 元忠姓名，朝廷所賜也，本姓曹，名令忠；

translations.literal: Yuanzhong's given name and surname were bestowed by the court; his original surname was Cao and his name Lingzhong;
translations.idiomatic: The name Yuanzhong had been granted by the court; his original surname was Cao and his given name Lingzhong;

sentences.zh: 昕，子儀弟之子也。

translations.literal: Xin was the son of Ziyi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was a son of Guo Ziyi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 李希烈以久雨未進軍，上怪之，盧杞密言於上曰：「希烈遷延，以楊炎故也。

translations.literal: Li Xilie, because of prolonged rain, had not advanced his army; the emperor found it strange. Lu Qi spoke secretly to the emperor, saying: "Xilie delays because of Yang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie had not marched because of unending rain, and the emperor was puzzled. Lu Qi said privately to him, "Xilie is stalling on account of Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 陛下何愛炎一日之名而墮大功？

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty cherish Yan's title for a single day and ruin a great achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Why cling to Yan's title for one day and sacrifice a great victory?

sentences.zh: 不若暫免炎相以悅之。

translations.literal: Better to remove Yan from the chancellorship for a time to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Better to remove Yan from the chancellorship for the moment and placate him.

sentences.zh: 事平復用，無傷也。」

translations.literal: When the affair is settled, employ him again—no harm done."
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign is over, restore him—no harm done."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以炎為左僕射，罷政事。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Yan was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and removed from active governance.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day, Yan was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and dismissed from the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以前永平節度使張鎰為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The former military commissioner of Yongping, Zhang Yi, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, former military commissioner of Yongping, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 鎰，齊丘之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a son of Qiqiu.

sentences.zh: 以朔方節度使崔寧為右僕射。

translations.literal: Cui Ning, military commissioner of Shuofang, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning, military commissioner of Shuofang, was appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丙子，贈故伊州刺史袁光庭工部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the former prefect of Yizhou, Yuan Guangting, was posthumously given the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day, Yuan Guangting, former prefect of Yizhou, was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光庭天寶末為伊州刺史，吐蕃陷河、隴，光庭堅守累年，吐蕃百方誘之，不下。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era Guangting was prefect of Yizhou; when the Tibetans took He and Long, Guangting held firm for years while the Tibetans tried every means to entice him—he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Tianbao period Guangting served as prefect of Yizhou; when the Tibetans overran He and Long, he held the city for years while they tried every inducement to win him over—he would not surrender.

sentences.zh: 糧竭兵盡，城且陷，光庭先殺妻子，然後自焚。

translations.literal: When grain was exhausted and troops spent, and the city was about to fall, Guangting first killed his wife and children, then burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies ran out and his men were spent, with the city on the verge of capture, Guangting killed his wife and children and then burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 郭昕使至，朝廷始知之，故贈官。

translations.literal: When Guo Xin's envoy arrived, the court learned of it for the first time and therefore granted the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Guo Xin's envoy reached the capital did the court learn of his fate, and the posthumous honor was granted.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以邠寧節度使李懷光兼朔方節度使。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Li Huaiguang, military commissioner of Binning, was additionally made military commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, Li Huaiguang, commissioner of Binning, was also given command of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 癸未，河東節度使馬燧，昭義節度使李抱真，神策先鋒都知兵馬使李晟，大破田悅於臨洺。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Ma Sui, military commissioner of Hedong, Li Baozhen, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, and Li Sheng, forward commander of the Shence Army, inflicted a great defeat on Tian Yue at Linzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day, Ma Sui of Hedong, Li Baozhen of Zhaoyi, and Li Sheng, forward commander of the Shence forces, won a crushing victory over Tian Yue at Linzhou.

sentences.zh: 時悅攻臨洺，累月不拔，城中食且盡，府庫竭，士卒多死傷。

translations.literal: At that time Yue had been attacking Linzhou for months without taking it; food in the city was nearly gone, the treasuries were empty, and many soldiers had been killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had besieged Linzhou for months without success; provisions were running out, the treasury was bare, and casualties mounted among the defenders.

sentences.zh: 張伾飾其愛女，使出拜將士曰：「諸群守戰甚苦，伾家無它物，請鬻此女為將士一日之費。」

translations.literal: Zhang Pi adorned his beloved daughter and had her come out to bow to the troops, saying: "You all have suffered greatly in defending the city; Pi's household has nothing else—please sell this daughter to provide one day's expenses for the soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi dressed his beloved daughter and brought her before the troops, saying, "You have borne great hardship in this defense; my household has nothing else—I beg you to sell my daughter to pay one day's rations for the garrison."

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭，曰：「願盡死力，不敢言賞！」

translations.literal: All wept and said, "We wish to give our utmost strength—we dare not speak of reward!"
translations.idiomatic: All wept and cried, "We will fight to the death—we want no reward!"

sentences.zh: 李抱真告急於朝，詔馬燧將步騎二萬與抱真討悅，又遣李晟將神策兵與之俱；

translations.literal: Li Baozhen reported the emergency to court; the emperor ordered Ma Sui to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to join Baozhen in attacking Yue, and also sent Li Sheng with the Shence troops to accompany them;
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen sent urgent word to the capital; the emperor ordered Ma Sui to march twenty thousand foot and horse to join Baozhen against Yue, and dispatched Li Sheng with the Shence army as well;

sentences.zh: 又詔幽州留後朱滔討惟岳。

translations.literal: he also ordered Zhu Tao, acting commissioner of Youzhou, to attack Wei Yue.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Zhu Tao, acting commissioner of Youzhou, to move against Li Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 燧等軍未出險，先遣使持書諭悅，為好語。

translations.literal: Before Sui's army had even cleared the passes, he first sent envoys with letters to instruct Yue in conciliatory terms.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ma Sui's army had even left the mountain passes, he sent envoys bearing conciliatory messages to Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅謂燧畏之，不設備，又與抱真合兵八萬，東下壺關，軍於邯鄲，擊悅支軍，破之。

translations.literal: Yue thought Sui feared him and made no preparations; Sui then joined Baozhen with eighty thousand men, marched east through Huguan, encamped at Handan, and struck Yue's detached force, defeating it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue concluded that Ma Sui was afraid of him and took no precautions; Ma Sui then united with Baozhen for eighty thousand men, descended east through Huguan, encamped at Handan, and routed Yue's detached column.

sentences.zh: 悅方急攻臨洺，分李惟岳兵五千助楊朝光。

translations.literal: Yue was pressing the assault on Linzhou and had detached five thousand of Li Weiyue's troops to assist Yang Chaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: While Yue was pressing the siege of Linzhou, he detached five thousand of Li Weiyue's troops to reinforce Yang Chaoguang.

sentences.zh: 明日，燧等進攻朝光柵，悅將萬餘人救之，燧命大將李自良等御之於雙岡，令之曰：「悅得過，必斬爾！」

translations.literal: The next day Sui and the others attacked Chaoguang's stockade; Yue led more than ten thousand men to the rescue, and Sui ordered the great generals Li Ziliang and others to block them at Shuanggang, saying: "If Yue gets through, I shall behead you!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ma Sui attacked Chaoguang's camp; Yue brought more than ten thousand men to relieve it, and Ma Sui ordered Li Ziliang and other senior commanders to hold Shuanggang, saying, "If Yue breaks through, I will behead you all!"

sentences.zh: 自良等力戰，悅軍卻。

translations.literal: Ziliang and the others fought fiercely and Yue's army fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang and his men fought hard and drove Yue's forces back.

sentences.zh: 燧推火車焚朝光柵，斬朝光，獲首虜五千餘級。

translations.literal: Sui pushed fire carts to burn Chaoguang's stockade, beheaded Chaoguang, and took more than five thousand heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui rolled up fire wagons to burn the camp, killed Chaoguang, and took more than five thousand heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 居五日，燧等進軍至臨洺，悅悉眾力戰，凡百餘合，悅兵大敗，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: After five days Sui and the others advanced to Linzhou; Yue mustered all his forces and fought hard for more than a hundred engagements—Yue's army was utterly defeated and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Ma Sui marched on Linzhou; Yue threw in his entire army and fought through more than a hundred clashes—his force was shattered and over ten thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 悅引兵夜遁，邢州圍亦解。

translations.literal: Yue withdrew his army by night in flight, and the siege of Xingzhou was also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue fled by night with his army, and the siege of Xingzhou was raised.

sentences.zh: 時平盧節度使李正己已薨，子納秘之，擅領軍務。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhengji, military commissioner of Pinglu, had already died; his son Na kept it secret and seized control of military affairs on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji, military commissioner of Pinglu, had already died; his son Li Na concealed the death and took command on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 悅求救於納及李惟岳，納遣大將衛俊將兵萬人，惟岳遣兵三千人救之。

translations.literal: Yue begged Na and Li Weiyue for aid; Na sent the great general Wei Jun with ten thousand troops, and Weiyue sent three thousand men to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue appealed to Li Na and Li Weiyue for help; Na dispatched Wei Jun with ten thousand men, and Weiyue sent three thousand.

sentences.zh: 悅收合散卒，得二萬餘人，軍於洹水；

translations.literal: Yue gathered his scattered soldiers and mustered more than twenty thousand, encamping on the Huan River;
translations.idiomatic: Yue rallied his broken forces to more than twenty thousand and encamped on the Huan River;

sentences.zh: 淄青軍其東，成德軍其西，首尾相應。

translations.literal: the Ziqing army was to his east and the Chengde army to his west, head and tail answering each other.
translations.idiomatic: with the Ziqing army to his east and the Chengde army to his west, the two wings supporting each other.

sentences.zh: 馬燧帥諸軍進屯鄴，奏求河陽兵自助；

translations.literal: Ma Sui led the various armies forward and encamped at Ye, memorializing to request Heyang troops to reinforce him;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui advanced and encamped at Ye, requesting Heyang reinforcements in a memorial;

sentences.zh: 詔河陽節度使李艽將兵會之。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered Li Wan, military commissioner of Heyang, to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered Li Wan, commissioner of Heyang, to march and join him.

sentences.zh: 八月，李納始發喪，奏請襲父位，上不許。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Li Na at last announced the mourning; he memorialized to request succession to his father's post, and the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Na finally announced his father's death and petitioned to succeed him; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義發兵至江陵，至四望，大敗而歸，乃收兵襄、鄧。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi sent troops to Jiangling; at Siwang they were utterly defeated and returned, then gathered their forces back at Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi marched toward Jiangling but was routed at Siwang and withdrew, concentrating his forces at Xiangyang and Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 李希烈引軍循漢而上，與諸道兵會；

translations.literal: Li Xilie led his army up the Han River and joined the forces of the various circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie marched up the Han and united with the armies of the other circuits;

sentences.zh: 崇義遣其將翟暉、杜少誠逆戰於蠻水，希烈大破之；

translations.literal: Chongyi sent his generals Zhai Hui and Du Shaoqian to give battle at Manshui; Xilie inflicted a great defeat on them;
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi sent Zhai Hui and Du Shaoqian to meet them at Manshui; Xilie crushed them;

sentences.zh: 追至疏口，又破之。

translations.literal: pursued them to Shukou and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: pursued them to Shukou and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 二將請降，希烈使將其眾先入襄陽慰諭軍民。

translations.literal: The two generals asked to surrender; Xilie had them lead their troops first into Xiangyang to reassure the army and people.
translations.idiomatic: Both generals offered to surrender; Xilie sent them ahead with their men into Xiangyang to reassure the garrison and populace.

sentences.zh: 崇義閉城拒守，守者開門爭出，不可禁。

translations.literal: Chongyi shut the city and held out, but the defenders opened the gates and scrambled to get out—it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi barred the gates to resist, but the defenders threw them open and rushed out in a panic that no one could halt.

sentences.zh: 崇義與妻赴井死，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Chongyi and his wife threw themselves into a well and died; his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi and his wife drowned themselves in a well; his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 范陽節度使朱滔將討李惟岳，軍於莫州。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao, military commissioner of Fanyang, was about to attack Li Weiyue and encamped at Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, military commissioner of Fanyang, prepared to attack Li Weiyue and encamped at Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 張孝忠將精兵八千守易州，滔遣判官蔡雄說孝忠曰：「惟岳乳臭兒，敢拒朝命；

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaozhong held Yizhou with eight thousand elite troops; Tao sent his aide Cai Xiong to persuade Xiaozhong, saying: "Weiyue is a milk-smelling boy who dares defy the court's command;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong garrisoned Yizhou with eight thousand picked troops; Zhu Tao sent his aide Cai Xiong to win him over, saying, "Weiyue is a callow boy who dares defy the throne;

sentences.zh: 今昭義、河東軍已破田悅，淮寧李僕射克襄陽，計河南諸軍，朝夕北向，恆、魏之亡，可佇立而須也。

translations.literal: now the armies of Zhaoyi and Hedong have already defeated Tian Yue, and Vice Minister Li of Huaining has taken Xiangyang; counting the armies of Henan, they will turn north before long—the fall of Heng and Wei can be awaited standing still.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhaoyi and Hedong armies have already broken Tian Yue, and Vice Minister Li of Huaining has taken Xiangyang; the Henan forces will march north any day now—the fall of Heng and Wei is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 使君誠能首舉易州以歸朝廷，則破惟岳之功自使君始，此轉禍為福之策也。」

translations.literal: If you, my lord, can be the first to raise Yizhou and return it to the court, then the merit of destroying Weiyue will begin with you—this is the strategy of turning misfortune into blessing."
translations.idiomatic: If you would be first to surrender Yizhou to the court, the credit for destroying Weiyue will be yours—this is how you turn disaster into advantage."

sentences.zh: 孝忠然之，遣牙官程華詣滔，遣錄事參軍董稹奉表詣闕，滔又上表薦之。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong agreed; he sent his gate officer Cheng Hua to Tao and his recording secretary Dong Zhi to present a memorial at court; Tao also submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong agreed; he sent Cheng Hua to Zhu Tao and Dong Zhi to the capital with a submission of allegiance; Zhu Tao also memorialized in his favor.

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛酉，以孝忠為成德節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinyou, Xiaozhong was made military commissioner of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the xinyou day, Zhang Xiaozhong was appointed military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 命惟岳護喪歸朝，惟岳不從。

translations.literal: Weiyue was ordered to escort the coffin to court; Weiyue would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weiyue was ordered to bring his father's coffin to court; he refused.

sentences.zh: 孝忠德滔，為子茂和娶滔女，深相結。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong was grateful to Tao; he had his son Maohe marry Tao's daughter, and they bound themselves deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful to Zhu Tao, Xiaozhong had his son Maohe marry Tao's daughter, and the two men became close allies.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，加李希烈同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Li Xilie was given the additional title of Associate Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day, Li Xilie was made Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，李希烈請討梁崇義，上對朝士亟稱其忠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Xilie had asked to attack Liang Chongyi, the emperor had repeatedly praised his loyalty to the courtiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie had first volunteered to attack Liang Chongyi, the emperor had repeatedly praised his loyalty before the court.

sentences.zh: 黜陟使李承自淮西還，言於上曰：「希烈必立微功；

translations.literal: The inspection commissioner Li Cheng, returning from Huaixi, said to the emperor: "Xilie will certainly win some small merit;
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, the inspection commissioner, returning from Huaixi, told the emperor, "Xilie will no doubt win some modest success;

sentences.zh: 但恐有功之後，偃蹇不臣，更煩朝廷用兵耳。」

translations.literal: but I fear that after he has merit he will grow arrogant and refuse to serve, and the court will have to send troops again."
translations.idiomatic: but I fear that once he has a victory he will grow insolent and defiant, and the court will have to fight him all over again."

sentences.zh: 上不以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor did not think so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed the warning.

sentences.zh: 希烈既得襄陽，遂據之為己有，上乃思承言。

translations.literal: Once Xilie had taken Xiangyang, he seized it as his own; only then did the emperor recall Cheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie took Xiangyang he kept it for himself, and the emperor remembered what Li Cheng had said.

sentences.zh: 時承為河中尹，甲子，以承為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: At that time Cheng was prefect of Hezhong; on the day jiazi he was made military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was then prefect of Hezhong; on the jiazi day he was appointed military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上欲以禁兵送上，承請單騎赴鎮。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to send him with palace troops, but Cheng asked to go to his post alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered him an imperial guard escort, but Cheng asked to ride to his post alone.

sentences.zh: 至襄陽，希烈置之外館，迫脅萬方，承誓死不屈，希烈乃大掠闔境所有而去。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangyang, Xilie lodged him in an outer guesthouse and pressed him in every way; Cheng swore to die rather than yield, and Xilie then plundered everything in the entire circuit and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang, Xilie quartered him in an outer lodge and tried every form of coercion; Cheng vowed to die rather than submit, whereupon Xilie looted the entire circuit and marched away.

sentences.zh: 承治之期年，軍府稍完。

translations.literal: After a full year of Cheng's administration, the military government was gradually restored.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year of Li Cheng's rule, the military administration was largely restored.

sentences.zh: 希烈留牙將於襄州，守其所掠財，由是數有使者往來。

translations.literal: Xilie left a gate officer at Xiangzhou to guard the goods he had plundered; hence envoys went back and forth frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie left a deputy at Xiangzhou to guard his plunder, and envoys shuttled between them with increasing frequency.

sentences.zh: 承亦遣其腹心臧叔雅往來許、蔡，厚結希烈腹心周曾等，與之陰圖希烈。

translations.literal: Cheng also sent his confidant Zang Shuya back and forth between Xu and Cai, cultivating close ties with Xilie's inner circle Zhou Zeng and others, and with them secretly plotted against Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent his trusted agent Zang Shuya to travel between Xu and Cai, winning over Xilie's confidants such as Zhou Zeng and plotting with them to bring Xilie down.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭嵩家廟臨曲江，玄宗以娛游之地，非神靈所宅，命徙之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Song's family temple overlooked Qujiang; Emperor Xuanzong, holding that an amusement ground was no dwelling for spirits, ordered it moved.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Xiao Song's ancestral temple had stood above Qujiang; Emperor Xuanzong, deeming a pleasure ground unfit for the spirits, ordered it relocated.

sentences.zh: 楊炎為相，惡京兆尹嚴郢，左遷大理卿。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan was chancellor he hated the metropolitan prefect Yan Ying and demoted him to chief judge of the Grand Court.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Yan was chancellor he took against Yan Ying, the metropolitan prefect, and transferred him to chief judge of the Grand Court.

sentences.zh: 盧杞欲陷炎，引郢為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Lu Qi wished to destroy Yan and brought Yan Ying back as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, seeking to ruin Yang Yan, recalled Yan Ying as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先是，炎將營家廟，有宅在東都，憑河南尹趙惠伯賣之，惠伯買以為官廨，郢按之，以為有羨利。

translations.literal: Earlier Yan had planned to build a family temple; he had a residence in the eastern capital and relied on Henan Prefect Zhao Huibo to sell it—Huibo bought it for government offices; Yan Ying investigated and found unfair profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been preparing to build a family temple and had a house in the eastern capital that he asked Henan Prefect Zhao Huibo to sell; Huibo bought it for official use, and Yan Ying's investigation found illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 杞召大理正田晉議法，晉以為：「律，監臨官市買有羨利，以乞取論，當奪官。」

translations.literal: Qi summoned Grand Court reviewer Tian Jin to discuss the law; Jin held: "By statute, when a supervisory official profits in a purchase, it is judged as extortion and office should be stripped."
translations.idiomatic: Qi called in Grand Court reviewer Tian Jin to interpret the law; Jin argued that when a supervisory official profited on a purchase, the statute treated it as extortion and required removal from office."

sentences.zh: 杞怒，貶晉衡州司馬。

translations.literal: Qi was angry and demoted Jin to military adjutant of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was furious and demoted Jin to adjutant of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 更召它吏議法，以為：「監主自盜，罪當絞。」

translations.literal: He summoned other officials to discuss the law and found: "When a supervisor steals on his own authority, the crime warrants strangulation."
translations.idiomatic: He called in other officials, who ruled that a supervising official who stole on his own authority should be strangled."

sentences.zh: 炎廟正直蕭嵩廟地，杞因譖炎，云「茲地有王氣，故玄宗令嵩徙之。

translations.literal: Yan's temple stood on the site of Xiao Song's former temple; Qi slandered Yan, saying: "This ground has imperial aura—hence Xuanzong had Song move his temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's temple stood on the former site of Xiao Song's shrine; Qi denounced him, saying, "This ground bears royal qi—that is why Xuanzong made Song move away.

sentences.zh: 炎有異志，故於其地建廟。」

translations.literal: Yan harbored treacherous intent and therefore built his temple on that site."
translations.idiomatic: Yan harbors treasonous designs and built his temple there on purpose."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙未，炎自左僕射貶崖州司馬。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day yimao, Yan was demoted from Left Vice Director to military adjutant of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the yimao day, Yan was demoted from Left Vice Director to adjutant of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 遣中使護送，未至崖州百里，縊殺之。

translations.literal: A palace envoy was sent to escort him; a hundred li before Yazhou he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy escorted him; a hundred li short of Yazhou he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 惠伯自河中尹貶費州多田尉。

translations.literal: Huibo was demoted from prefect of Hezhong to captain of Duotian in Feizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo was demoted from prefect of Hezhong to captain of Duotian in Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋亦殺之。

translations.literal: Soon he too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，冊太子妃蕭氏。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Lady Xiao was invested as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, Lady Xiao was formally installed as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，祫太廟。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the subsumption sacrifice was performed at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, the subsumption rite was held at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖既正東向之位，獻、懿二祖皆藏西夾室，不饗。

translations.literal: Earlier, once Taizu had taken the east-facing position, the Xian and Yi ancestors were stored in the western side chambers and not offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, after Taizu was given the east-facing seat, the Xian and Yi ancestors had been placed in the western side chambers and went without offerings.

sentences.zh: 至是，復奉獻祖東向而饗之。

translations.literal: Now the Xian ancestor was again placed east-facing and offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Xian ancestor was restored to the east-facing place and honored once more.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史李洧，正己之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Li Wei, prefect of Xuzhou, was a cousin of Zhengji on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, prefect of Xuzhou, was a paternal cousin of Li Zhengji.

sentences.zh: 李納寇宋州，彭城令太原白季庚說洧舉州歸國。

translations.literal: Li Na raided Songzhou; Bai Jigeng of Taiyuan, magistrate of Pengcheng, urged Wei to submit the whole prefecture to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na attacked Songzhou, Pengcheng magistrate Bai Jigeng urged Li Wei to bring the entire prefecture back to imperial allegiance.

sentences.zh: 洧從之，遣攝巡官崔程奉表詣闕，且使口奏，並白宰相，以「徐州不能獨抗納，乞領徐、海、沂三州觀察使，況海、沂二州，今皆為納有。

translations.literal: Wei agreed and sent acting inspector Cui Cheng with a memorial to court, also an oral report to the chancellors, saying: "Xuzhou cannot resist Na alone; I beg to be made observer of Xu, Hai, and Yi—moreover Hai and Yi are now both held by Na.
translations.idiomatic: Wei agreed and sent Cui Cheng with a memorial to the capital and an oral message to the chancellors: "Xuzhou cannot stand alone against Li Na; I ask to be made observer of Xu, Hai, and Yi—Hai and Yi are already in Na's hands.

sentences.zh: 洧與刺史王涉、馬萬通素有約，苟得朝廷詔書，必能成功。」

translations.literal: Wei had long had an agreement with prefects Wang She and Ma Wantong; if he could obtain an imperial edict, success was certain."
translations.idiomatic: Wei had long been in league with the prefects Wang She and Ma Wantong; with an imperial edict in hand, he was confident of success."

sentences.zh: 程自外來，以為宰相一也，先白張鎰，鎰以告盧杞。

translations.literal: Cheng, coming from outside, thought all chancellors were the same and first reported to Zhang Yi; Yi told Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, arriving from the provinces, assumed all chancellors were alike and reported first to Zhang Yi, who passed the word to Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 杞怒其不先白己，不從其請。

translations.literal: Qi was angry that he had not reported to him first and refused the request.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was furious that Cheng had not come to him first and rejected the petition.

sentences.zh: 戊申，加洧御史大夫，充招諭使。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Wei was made Censor-in-Chief and appointed pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, Li Wei was made Censor-in-Chief and imperial pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊午，以永樂公主適檢校比部郎中田華，上不欲違先志故也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day wuwu, Princess Yongle was married to Tian Hua, acting director of the Bureau of Review—because the emperor did not wish to violate his predecessor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the wuwu day, Princess Yongle was married to Tian Hua of the Bureau of Review—the emperor would not go against his father's wish.

sentences.zh: 蜀王傀，更名遂。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu, Kui, changed his name to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu, Kui, took the new name Sui.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，宣武節度使劉洽，神策都知兵馬使曲環，滑州刺史襄平李澄，朔方大將唐朝臣，大破淄青、魏博之兵於徐州。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Liu He, military commissioner of Xuanwu, Qu Huan, commander of the Shence Army, Li Cheng of Xiangping, prefect of Huazhou, and Tang Chaochen, great general of Shuofang, inflicted a great defeat on the Ziqing and Weibo armies at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, Liu He of Xuanwu, Qu Huan of the Shence Army, Li Cheng of Huazhou, and Tang Chaochen of Shuofang won a crushing victory over the Ziqing and Weibo forces at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，李納遣其將王溫會魏博將信都崇慶共攻徐州，李洧遣牙官溫人王智興詣闕告急。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Na had sent his general Wang Wen to join Weibo general Xindu Chongqing in attacking Xuzhou; Li Wei sent his gate officer Wang Zhixing of Wen to the capital to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na had sent Wang Wen and the Weibo commander Xindu Chongqing to besiege Xuzhou; Li Wei dispatched Wang Zhixing of Wen to the capital for help.

sentences.zh: 智興善走，不五日而至。

translations.literal: Zhixing was a fast runner and arrived in less than five days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing was famed for his speed and reached the capital in under five days.

sentences.zh: 上為之發朔方兵五千人，以朝臣將之，與洽、環、澄共救之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched five thousand Shuofang troops with Tang Chaochen in command to join He, Huan, and Cheng in the relief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent five thousand Shuofang troops under Tang Chaochen to join Liu He, Qu Huan, and Li Cheng in the relief.

sentences.zh: 時朔方軍資裝不至，旗服弊惡。

translations.literal: At that time the Shuofang army's supplies and equipment had not arrived; their banners and uniforms were worn and shabby.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang column had not yet received its supplies; their banners and uniforms were ragged.

sentences.zh: 宣武人嗤之曰：「乞子能破賊乎！」

translations.literal: The men of Xuanwu mocked them, saying: "Can beggars break the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanwu troops mocked them: "Can beggars beat an army?"

sentences.zh: 朝臣以其言激怒士卒，且曰：「都統有令，先破賊營者，營中物悉與之。」

translations.literal: Chaochen, taking their words as an insult to his soldiers, also said: "The commander-in-chief has ordered: whoever first breaks the enemy camp shall have everything in that camp."
translations.idiomatic: Chaochen, stung by the taunt on behalf of his men, added, "The commander has promised: whoever breaks the enemy camp first keeps everything in it."

sentences.zh: 士皆憤怒爭奮。

translations.literal: The soldiers were all furious and strove eagerly.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang soldiers burned with anger and fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 崇慶、溫攻彭城，二旬不能下，請益兵於納。

translations.literal: Chongqing and Wen attacked Pengcheng but could not take it in twenty days and asked Na for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing and Wen besieged Pengcheng for twenty days without success and asked Li Na for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 納遣其將石隱金將萬人助之，與劉洽等相拒於七里溝。

translations.literal: Na sent his general Shi Yinjian with ten thousand men to assist them, and they faced Liu He and the others at Qiligou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na sent Shi Yinjian with ten thousand men; the two sides faced off at Qiligou against Liu He and his allies.

sentences.zh: 日向暮，洽引軍稍卻。

translations.literal: As the day drew toward evening, He drew his army back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Near dusk, Liu He pulled his line back a little.

sentences.zh: 朔方馬軍使楊朝晟言於唐朝臣曰：「公以步兵負山而陳，以待兩軍。

translations.literal: Yang Chaosheng, cavalry commander of Shuofang, said to Tang Chaochen: "You array your infantry with the mountain at their backs and wait for both armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaosheng, the Shuofang cavalry commander, told Tang Chaochen, "Post your infantry with the mountain behind them and hold both wings.

sentences.zh: 我以騎兵伏於山曲，賊見懸軍勢孤，必搏之。

translations.literal: I shall hide cavalry in the mountain bend; when the enemy sees an isolated army they will surely attack.
translations.idiomatic: I will hide the cavalry in the bend of the hills; when they see a lone force they will charge.

sentences.zh: 我以伏兵絕其腰，必敗之。」

translations.literal: With ambush troops I shall cut them in the middle—they will surely be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: My ambush will cut them in half—we are sure to win."

sentences.zh: 朝臣從之。

translations.literal: Chaochen followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chaochen agreed.

sentences.zh: 崇慶等果將騎二千逾橋而西，追擊官軍，伏兵發，橫擊之。

translations.literal: Chongqing and the others did lead two thousand cavalry west over the bridge in pursuit of the government army; the ambush sprang and struck them from the flank.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing duly led two thousand horsemen west over the bridge in pursuit; the ambush rose and struck them from the side.

sentences.zh: 崇慶等兵中斷，狼狽而返，阻橋以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Chongqing's force was cut in two and fled in disorder, blocking the bridge to hold off the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Their column was cut in two and fled in disorder, holding the bridge against the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 其兵有爭橋不得，涉水而度者。

translations.literal: Some of their soldiers, unable to win the bridge, waded across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Some who could not reach the bridge waded the stream instead.

sentences.zh: 朝晟指之曰：「彼可涉，吾何為不涉！」

translations.literal: Chaosheng pointed at them and said: "They can ford it—why should we not ford it!"
translations.idiomatic: Chaosheng pointed and cried, "If they can cross, why can't we!"

sentences.zh: 遂涉水擊，據橋者皆走，崇慶等兵大潰。

translations.literal: He forded the water and attacked; those holding the bridge all fled, and Chongqing's army was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: He waded across and charged; the men on the bridge scattered, and Chongqing's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 洽等乘之，斬首八千級，溺死過半。

translations.literal: He and the others pressed the pursuit, taking eight thousand heads; more than half drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He pressed the pursuit, taking eight thousand heads; more than half drowned in the stream.

sentences.zh: 朔方軍士盡得其輜重，旗服鮮華，乃謂宣武人曰：「乞子之功，孰與宋多？」

translations.literal: The Shuofang soldiers obtained all their baggage; their banners and uniforms were fresh and splendid, and they said to the men of Xuanwu: "How does the merit of beggars compare with that of Song?"
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang troops took all the enemy baggage and now rode under bright banners; they asked the Xuanwu men, "Whose victory was greater—beggars or Song men?"

sentences.zh: 宣武人皆慚。

translations.literal: The men of Xuanwu were all ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanwu troops were shamed into silence.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘勝逐北，至徐州城下，魏博、淄青軍解圍走，江、淮漕運始通。

translations.literal: The government army pursued the victory north to the walls of Xuzhou; the Weibo and Ziqing armies lifted the siege and fled, and transport on the Jiang and Huai was opened at last.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army pursued to the walls of Xuzhou; the Weibo and Ziqing forces broke off the siege and fled, and the Jiang-Huai grain route was open again.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔削李惟岳官爵；

translations.literal: On the day jisi, an edict stripped Li Weiyue of office and rank;
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, an edict stripped Li Weiyue of his titles and offices;

sentences.zh: 募所部降者，赦而賞之。

translations.literal: those under his command who surrendered were to be pardoned and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: and promised pardon and reward to any of his followers who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 甲申，淮南節度使陳少游遣兵擊海州，其刺史王涉以州降。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Chen Shaoyou, military commissioner of Huainan, sent troops to attack Haizhou; its prefect Wang She surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day, Chen Shaoyou of Huainan attacked Haizhou, and prefect Wang She surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李納密州刺史馬萬通乞降；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Ma Wantong, prefect of Mizhou under Li Na, asked to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Ma Wantong, Li Na's prefect of Mizhou, offered to surrender;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以為密州刺史。

translations.literal: on the day dingyou he was made prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: and on the dingyou day was confirmed as prefect of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 崔漢衡至吐蕃，贊普以敕書稱貢獻及賜，全以臣禮見處。

translations.literal: Cui Hanheng reached Tibet; the khan treated the edicts' language of tribute and bestowal entirely with the ritual of subject and lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hanheng reached Tibet, the khan treated the imperial edicts—which spoke of tribute and gifts—as if he were receiving a subject, using the full ritual of lord and vassal.

sentences.zh: 又，雲州之西，當以賀蘭山為境，邀漢衡更請之。

translations.literal: Moreover, west of Yunzhou the border should run along the Helan Mountains; he pressed Hanheng to request this anew.
translations.idiomatic: He also insisted that the border west of Yunzhou should follow the Helan Mountains and pressed Hanheng to petition the court again.

sentences.zh: 丁未，漢衡遣判官與吐蕃使者入奏。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Hanheng sent his aide with Tibetan envoys to present a memorial at court.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, Hanheng sent his aide with Tibetan envoys to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上為之改敕書、境土，皆如其請。

translations.literal: The emperor altered the edicts and the border territory all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revised the edicts and the frontier boundaries to match every demand.

sentences.zh: 加馬燧魏博招討使。

translations.literal: Ma Sui was additionally made pacification commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui was also appointed pacification commissioner for Weibo.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝二建中三年（

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong of Emperor Dezong, the Sagacious, Martial, and Sagely Text Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong under Emperor Dezong, the Sagacious Martial and Literarily Accomplished Emperor (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元七八二年）

translations.literal: renxu, corresponding to the year 782 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the renxu year, equivalent to 782 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，河陽節度使李艽引兵逼衛州，田悅守將任履虛詐降，既而復叛。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Li Wan, military commissioner of Heyang, led troops to press Weizhou; Tian Yue's defending general Ren Lüxu feigned surrender and then rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Li Wan of Heyang advanced on Weizhou; Tian Yue's garrison commander Ren Lüxu pretended to surrender and then rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 馬燧等諸軍屯於漳濱。

translations.literal: Ma Sui and the various armies encamped on the Zhang River bank.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and the allied armies encamped along the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 田悅遣其將王光進築月城以守長橋，諸軍不得渡。

translations.literal: Tian Yue sent his general Wang Guangjin to build crescent ramparts to hold the long bridge, and the armies could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue sent Wang Guangjin to build crescent ramparts defending the long bridge, blocking the imperial crossing.

sentences.zh: 燧以鐵鎖連車數百乘，實以土囊，塞其下流，水淺，諸軍涉渡。

translations.literal: Sui linked several hundred carts with iron chains, filled them with earth bags, and dammed the downstream; the water grew shallow and the armies waded across.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui chained hundreds of carts with iron cables, filled them with earth bags, and dammed the lower stream until the water fell low enough for the armies to ford.

sentences.zh: 時軍中乏糧，悅等深壁不戰。

translations.literal: At that time the army lacked grain; Yue and the others held deep within their walls and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were short in the imperial camp; Yue and his allies stayed behind their walls and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 燧命諸軍持十日糧，進屯倉口，與悅夾洹水而軍。

translations.literal: Sui ordered the armies to carry ten days' rations, advanced to encamp at Cangkou, and faced Yue across the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui ordered each army to carry ten days' grain, advanced to Cangkou, and encamped facing Yue across the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 李抱真、李艽問曰：「糧少而深入，何也？」

translations.literal: Li Baozhen and Li Wan asked: "With little grain and a deep advance—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen and Li Wan asked, "Why advance so deep with so little grain?"

sentences.zh: 燧曰：「糧少則利速戰，今三鎮連兵不戰，欲以老我師。

translations.literal: Sui said: "Little grain favors swift battle. Now the three circuits have joined forces and will not fight—they wish to wear down our army.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui replied, "Scant grain forces a quick fight. The three rebel circuits are united and refuse battle—they mean to wear us down.

sentences.zh: 我若分軍擊其左右，悅必救之，則我腹背受敵，戰必不利。

translations.literal: If we divide our forces to strike their flanks, Yue will surely come to the rescue, and we shall be attacked front and rear—battle will surely go against us.
translations.idiomatic: If we split to strike their flanks, Yue will relieve them and catch us between two fires—that is how we lose.

sentences.zh: 故進軍逼悅，所謂攻其所必救也。

translations.literal: Therefore I advance to press Yue—what is called attacking what they must save.
translations.idiomatic: So I march straight at Yue—attack what they must defend.

sentences.zh: 彼苟出戰，必為諸君破之。」

translations.literal: If they come out to fight, I shall surely break them for you all."
translations.idiomatic: If they come out, you will break them for me."

sentences.zh: 乃為三橋逾洹水，日往挑戰，悅不出。

translations.literal: He then built three bridges over the Huan and went daily to offer challenge; Yue did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He built three bridges over the Huan and challenged Yue every day; Yue would not emerge.

sentences.zh: 燧令諸軍夜半起食，潛師循洹水直趨魏州，令曰：「賊至，則止為陳。」

translations.literal: Sui ordered the armies to rise at midnight and eat, then secretly marched along the Huan straight for Weizhou, with the order: "If the enemy comes, halt and form line."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui ordered the armies to rise and eat at midnight, then secretly marched along the Huan straight toward Weizhou. His order said, "If the enemy arrives, halt and form ranks."

sentences.zh: 留百騎擊鼓鳴角於營中，仍抱薪持火，俟諸軍畢，則止鼓角匿其旁。

translations.literal: He left a hundred cavalry to beat drums and blow horns in camp, still carrying firewood and torches; when all armies had passed, they stopped drums and horns and hid nearby.
translations.idiomatic: He left a hundred horsemen to drum and blow horns in the camp, with firewood and torches; when the main body had gone, they fell silent and hid nearby.

sentences.zh: 伺悅軍畢渡，焚其橋。

translations.literal: When Yue's army had finished crossing, they burned the bridges.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue's army had finished crossing, they burned the bridges.

sentences.zh: 軍行十里所，悅聞之，帥淄青、成德步騎四萬逾橋掩其後，乘風縱火，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: After the army had marched about ten li, Yue heard of it and led forty thousand infantry and cavalry of Ziqing and Chengde over the bridge to strike their rear, riding the wind to set fires and advancing with drums and shouts.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li into the march Yue learned of it and led forty thousand Ziqing and Chengde foot and horse over the bridges to strike the rear, fanning the wind to spread fire and charging with drums and shouts.

sentences.zh: 燧按兵不動，先除其前草莽百步為戰場，結陳以待之，募勇士五千餘人為前列。

translations.literal: Sui held his army still, first cleared the grass and brush a hundred paces ahead for a battlefield, formed line to await them, and recruited more than five thousand brave men for the front rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui held his line steady, cleared a hundred paces of brush for a battlefield, formed up to receive them, and picked five thousand stalwarts for the front rank.

sentences.zh: 悅軍至，火止，氣衰，燧縱岳擊之，悅軍大敗。

translations.literal: When Yue's army arrived the fires died and their spirit waned; Sui released the attack and Yue's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue's men arrived the flames died and their momentum faded; Ma Sui unleashed his attack and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 神策、昭義、河陽軍小卻，見河東軍捷，還鬥，又破之。

translations.literal: The Shence, Zhaoyi, and Heyang armies fell back slightly; seeing the Hedong army's victory they returned to fight and broke the enemy again.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence, Zhaoyi, and Heyang columns wavered; seeing the Hedong wing win, they rallied and broke the enemy again.

sentences.zh: 追奔至，三橋已焚，悅軍亂，赴水溺死不可勝紀，斬首二萬餘級，捕虜三千餘人，屍相枕藉三十餘里。

translations.literal: In the pursuit they reached the point where the three bridges had been burned; Yue's army was in chaos and countless drowned in the water; more than twenty thousand heads were taken and more than three thousand captives; corpses lay piled for more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached the burned bridges; Yue's army broke in panic and countless men drowned; over twenty thousand heads were taken and three thousand prisoners; corpses lay heaped for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 悅收餘兵千餘人走魏州。

translations.literal: Yue gathered the remnant of more than a thousand men and fled to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue rallied barely a thousand survivors and fled to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 馬燧與李抱真不協，頓兵平邑浮圖，遷延不進。

translations.literal: Ma Sui and Li Baozhen were not in harmony; he halted his army at the Pingyi pagoda and delayed, not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and Li Baozhen were at odds; Ma Sui halted at the Pingyi pagoda and lingered without advancing.

sentences.zh: 悅夜至南郭，大將李長春閉關不內，以俟官軍，久之，天且明，長春乃開門納之。

translations.literal: Yue reached the southern suburb by night; the great general Li Changchun closed the gate and would not admit him, waiting for the government army; after a long while, as dawn was near, Changchun at last opened the gate and let him in.
translations.idiomatic: Yue reached the south gate by night; Li Changchun barred the gate, hoping the imperial army would arrive first; only as dawn neared did he let Yue in.

sentences.zh: 悅殺長春，嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Yue killed Changchun and held the city in a desperate defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yue killed Changchun and shut himself in the city for a last stand.

sentences.zh: 城中士卒不滿數千，死者親戚，號哭滿街。

translations.literal: The soldiers in the city numbered fewer than several thousand; kin of the dead wailed until the streets were full of crying.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison numbered fewer than a few thousand; kin of the dead filled the streets with wailing.

sentences.zh: 悅憂懼，乃持佩刀，乘馬立府門外，悉集軍民，流涕言曰：「悅不肖，蒙淄青、成德二丈人大恩，不量其力，輒拒朝命，喪敗至此，使士大夫肝腦塗地，皆悅之罪也。

translations.literal: Yue, anxious and afraid, took his sword, mounted his horse, and stood outside the government gate; he gathered all soldiers and civilians and said through tears: "Yue is unworthy; I received great grace from the two lords of Ziqing and Chengde, misjudged my strength, and rashly defied the court's command, bringing defeat to this pass and causing officials and gentry to die in heaps—all Yue's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Worried and afraid, Yue took his sword, mounted his horse, and stood outside the government office gate. He gathered all the army and civilians and said through tears: "I, Yue, have been unworthy. I received great favor from the two elder lords of Ziqing and Chengde, misjudged my strength, and rashly defied the court's command. Defeat has come to this, and officers and gentlemen have had their brains smeared on the ground; all of it is my crime.

sentences.zh: 悅有老母，不能自殺，願諸公以此刀斷悅首，提出城降馬僕射，自取富貴，無為與悅俱死也！」

translations.literal: Yue has an old mother and cannot kill himself; I beg you all to use this sword to cut off Yue's head, take it out of the city, and surrender to Vice Minister Ma—win wealth and honor for yourselves, and do not die with Yue!"
translations.idiomatic: I have an aged mother and cannot kill myself—take this sword, cut off my head, carry it out, and surrender to Vice Minister Ma. Win your own fortune; do not die with me!"

sentences.zh: 因從馬上自投地。

translations.literal: With that he threw himself from the horse to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He flung himself from the saddle to the ground.

sentences.zh: 將士爭前抱持悅曰：「尚書舉兵徇義，非私己也。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers rushed forward to hold Yue, saying: "Minister, you raised troops for righteousness, not for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men rushed to hold him up, crying, "Minister, you took up arms for a just cause, not for yourself.

sentences.zh: 一勝一負，兵家之常。

translations.literal: One victory and one defeat are the constant of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Victory and defeat are the way of war.

sentences.zh: 某輩累世受恩，何忍聞此！

translations.literal: We have received grace for generations—how can we bear to hear this!
translations.idiomatic: Our families have owed you favor for generations—we cannot bear to hear this!

sentences.zh: 願奉尚書一戰，不勝則以死繼之。」

translations.literal: We wish to follow the Minister in one more battle; if we do not win, we shall follow with our deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Give us one more battle under your command; if we fail, we die with you."

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「諸公不以悅喪敗而棄之，悅雖死，敢忘厚意於地下！」

translations.literal: Yue said: "You do not abandon Yue because of defeat; though Yue die, how dare I forget your deep kindness in the grave!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "You do not abandon me in defeat; though I die, I shall not forget your loyalty below ground!"

sentences.zh: 乃與諸將各斷髮，約為兄弟，誓同生死。

translations.literal: He then cut his hair with each of the generals, swore brotherhood, and pledged life and death together.
translations.idiomatic: He and his generals each cut a lock of hair, swore brotherhood, and pledged to live or die together.

sentences.zh: 悉出府庫所有及斂富民之財，得百餘萬，以賞士卒，眾心始定。

translations.literal: He brought out everything in the government treasury and levied the wealth of rich households, obtaining more than a million, and used it to reward the soldiers; hearts were settled at last.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied the treasury and levied the rich for more than a million in cash, paid it out to the troops, and at last the garrison steadied.

sentences.zh: 復召貝州刺史刑曹俊，使之整部伍，繕守備，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: He again summoned Xing Caojun, prefect of Beizhou, had him put the ranks in order and repair the defenses, and the army's momentum revived.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue recalled Xing Caojun, prefect of Beizhou, to reorganize the ranks and shore up the defenses, and the army's fighting spirit returned.

sentences.zh: 李納軍於濮陽，為河南軍所逼，奔還濮州，征援兵於魏州。

translations.literal: Li Na had encamped at Puyang, was pressed by the Henan armies, fled back to Puzhou, and requested reinforcements from Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na had been camped at Puyang; driven back by the Henan forces, he withdrew to Puzhou and appealed to Weizhou for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 田悅遣軍使符璘將三百騎送之，璘父令奇謂璘曰：「吾老矣，歷觀安、史輩叛亂者，今皆安在！

translations.literal: Tian Yue sent the army commissioner Fu Lin with three hundred horsemen to escort them; Lin's father Lingqi said to Lin: "I am old; I have watched rebels of the An and Shi sort through the years—where are they all now!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue sent Fu Lin, an army commissioner, with three hundred cavalry to escort the column; Lin's father Lingqi told him, "I am old enough to have watched every rebel of the An Lushan and Shi Siming generation—where are they now?

sentences.zh: 田氏能久乎！

translations.literal: Can the Tian clan last long!
translations.idiomatic: Can the House of Tian endure?

sentences.zh: 汝因此棄逆從順，是汝揚父名於後世也。」

translations.literal: If you take this chance to abandon rebellion and follow loyalty, you will spread your father's name in later ages."
translations.idiomatic: Use this moment to turn from rebellion to obedience, and you will bring your father's name honor in generations to come."

sentences.zh: 嚙臂而別。

translations.literal: They bit their arms and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They bit their arms in farewell and parted.

sentences.zh: 璘遂與其副李瑤帥眾降於馬燧。

translations.literal: Lin then, with his deputy Li Yao, led the multitude to surrender to Ma Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin and his second Li Yao brought their men over to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 悅收族其家，令奇慢罵而死。

translations.literal: Yue exterminated his clan household; Lingqi died under slow abuse and curses.
translations.idiomatic: Yue wiped out the entire family and had Lingqi abused and reviled until he died.

sentences.zh: 瑤父再春以博州降，悅從兄昂以洺州降，王光進以長橋降。

translations.literal: Yao's father Zaichun surrendered Bozhou; Yue's cousin Ang surrendered Mingzhou; Wang Guangjin surrendered the Changqiao position.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yao's father Zaichun yielded Bozhou; Yue's kinsman Ang gave up Mingzhou; and Wang Guangjin handed over the Changqiao bridgehead.

sentences.zh: 悅入城旬餘日，馬燧等諸軍始至城下，攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Yue had entered the city for more than ten days when the various armies under Ma Sui and others at last reached below the walls, attacked, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue had been inside the city for a fortnight, Ma Sui and the allied armies at last arrived and assaulted the walls without success.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，李惟岳遣兵與孟祐守束鹿，朱滔、張孝忠攻拔之，進圍深州。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Li Weiyue sent troops with Meng You to hold Shulu; Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong stormed and took it, then advanced to besiege Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Li Weiyue sent Meng You to hold Shulu; Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong stormed the town and marched on to besiege Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟岳憂懼，掌書記邵真復說惟岳，密為表，先遣弟惟簡入朝；

translations.literal: Weiyue grew fearful; his secretary Shao Zhen again urged Weiyue, drafted a secret memorial, and first sent his younger brother Weijian to court;
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue was shaken with fear; his secretary Shao Zhen urged him again, drafted a secret memorial, and sent his younger brother Weijian to the capital first;

sentences.zh: 然後誅諸將之不從命者，身自入朝，使妻父冀州刺史鄭詵權知節度事，以待朝命。

translations.literal: then execute generals who disobeyed orders, go to court himself, have his father-in-law Zheng Shen, prefect of Jizhou, act as military commissioner pro tem pending court orders.
translations.idiomatic: then execute the disobedient generals, go to court in person, and leave his father-in-law Zheng Shen, prefect of Jizhou, as acting military commissioner until the throne decided his fate.

sentences.zh: 惟簡既行，孟祐知其謀，密遣告田悅。

translations.literal: Once Weijian had set out, Meng You learned of the plan and secretly reported it to Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Weijian was on the road, Meng You learned of the plot and secretly informed Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅大怒，使衙官扈岌往見惟岳，讓之曰：「尚書舉兵，正為大夫求旌節耳，非為己也。

translations.literal: Yue flew into a rage, sent his yamen officer Hu Ji to see Weiyue and rebuke him, saying: "The Senior Minister raised arms precisely to win a commission for you, the Lord—not for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was furious and sent his yamen officer Hu Ji to confront Weiyue: "Senior Minister Tian took up arms solely to win you a commission—not for his own sake.

sentences.zh: 今大夫乃信邵真之言，遣弟奉表，悉以反逆之罪歸尚書，自求雪身，尚書何負於大夫而至此邪！

translations.literal: Now you, Lord, trust Shao Zhen's words, send your brother with a memorial, lay all the crime of rebellion on the Senior Minister to clear yourself—what has the Senior Minister done to you that you come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Now you heed Shao Zhen, send your brother with a memorial, and lay every charge of rebellion on the Senior Minister to save your own skin—what has Tian done to deserve this from you!

sentences.zh: 若相為斬邵真，則相待如初；

translations.literal: If you together behead Shao Zhen, we can treat each other as before;
translations.idiomatic: If you will behead Shao Zhen with me, we can stand together as before;

sentences.zh: 不然，當與大夫絕矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise I must break with you, Lord.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I break with you entirely."

sentences.zh: 判官畢華言於惟岳曰：「田尚書以大夫之故陷身重圍，大夫一旦負之，不義甚矣。

translations.literal: Recorder Bi Hua said to Weiyue: "Senior Minister Tian because of you, Lord, is trapped in a heavy encirclement; for you suddenly to betray him is deeply unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Bi Hua told Weiyue, "Senior Minister Tian is trapped in a siege because of you; to turn on him now would be a gross betrayal.

sentences.zh: 且魏博、淄青兵強食富，足抗天下，事未可知，奈何遽為二三之計乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover Weibo and Ziqing are strong in troops and rich in grain—enough to stand against the empire; the outcome is still unknown—how can you rush into half measures!
translations.idiomatic: Weibo and Ziqing are strong and well supplied—enough to defy the empire. The outcome is still in doubt; why rush into half measures?"

sentences.zh: 惟岳素怯，不能守前計，乃引邵真，對扈岌斬之。

translations.literal: Weiyue was timid by nature, could not hold to his earlier plan; he summoned Shao Zhen and before Hu Ji beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue had always been timid; he could not hold to his earlier plan, summoned Shao Zhen, and beheaded him before Hu Ji.

sentences.zh: 發成德兵萬人，與孟祐俱圍束鹿。

translations.literal: He mobilized ten thousand Chengde troops and with Meng You jointly besieged Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: He raised ten thousand Chengde troops and with Meng You laid siege to Shulu again.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，朱滔、張孝忠與戰於束鹿城下，惟岳大敗，燒營而遁。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong fought beneath Shulu's walls; Weiyue was badly defeated, burned his camp, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Zhu Tao and Zhang Xiaozhong met Weiyue below Shulu; he was routed, burned his camp, and fled.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使王武俊為左右所構，惟岳疑之，惜其才，未忍除也。

translations.literal: Cavalry commander Wang Wujun was slandered by those around him; Weiyue grew suspicious yet treasured his talent and could not bring himself to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him had turned Weiyue against his cavalry commander Wang Wujun; he suspected Wujun but valued his ability and could not bring himself to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 束鹿之戰，使武俊為前鋒，私自謀曰：「我破朱滔，則惟岳軍勢大振，歸，殺我必矣。」

translations.literal: For the battle at Shulu he made Wujun vanguard; Wujun privately schemed, saying: "If I break Zhu Tao, Weiyue's armies will surge in power; when I return he is sure to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: At Shulu he put Wujun in the van; Wujun privately reasoned, "If I defeat Zhu Tao, Weiyue's armies will rally—and when I come home he will surely have me killed."

sentences.zh: 故戰不甚力而敗。

translations.literal: Hence he did not fight with full force and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: So he held back in the fight and lost.

sentences.zh: 朱滔欲乘勝攻恆州，張孝忠引兵西北，軍於義豐。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao wished to press the victory and attack Hengzhou; Zhang Xiaozhong led troops northwest and encamped at Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao meant to press on to Hengzhou, but Zhang Xiaozhong marched northwest and encamped at Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 滔大驚，孝忠將佐皆怪之，孝忠曰：「恆州宿將尚多，未易可輕。

translations.literal: Tao was greatly alarmed; Xiaozhong's officers all thought it strange; Xiaozhong said: "Hengzhou still has many veteran generals—it is not to be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was alarmed; Xiaozhong's officers were baffled. Xiaozhong said, "Hengzhou still has many seasoned commanders—it must not be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 迫之則並力死鬥，緩之則自相圖。

translations.literal: Press them and they will unite and fight to the death; relax pressure and they will plot against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Press them and they will unite and fight to the death; ease off and they will turn on one another.

sentences.zh: 諸君第觀之，吾軍義豐，坐待惟岳之殄滅耳。

translations.literal: Gentlemen, simply watch: with our army at Yifeng we can sit and await Weiyue's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Watch and wait: with our army at Yifeng we can sit out Weiyue's ruin.

sentences.zh: 且朱司徒言大而識淺，可與共始，難與共終也！」

translations.literal: Moreover Steward Zhu talks big but sees shallowly—one can start with him, hard to finish with him!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Steward Zhu talks big but sees little—you can begin with him, but not end with him!"

sentences.zh: 於是滔亦屯束鹿，不敢進。

translations.literal: At that Tao also camped at Shulu and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tao thereupon also halted at Shulu and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 惟岳將康日知以趙州歸國，惟岳益疑王武俊，武俊甚懼。

translations.literal: Weiyue's general Kang Rizhi brought Zhaozhou back to the empire; Weiyue grew still more suspicious of Wang Wujun, and Wujun was very afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue's general Kang Rizhi surrendered Zhaozhou to the throne; Weiyue grew still more suspicious of Wang Wujun, and Wujun was deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 或謂惟岳曰：「先相公委腹心於武俊，使之輔佐大夫，又有骨肉之親。

translations.literal: Someone said to Weiyue: "Your late father placed his inner trust in Wujun to assist you, Lord, and there is kinship by blood besides.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Weiyue, "Your late father entrusted Wujun to assist you, and you are kin besides.

sentences.zh: 武俊勇冠三軍，今危難之際，復加猜阻。

translations.literal: Wujun's valor tops the three armies; now in crisis you add suspicion and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's courage is unmatched in the army; now, in crisis, you add suspicion on top of it.

sentences.zh: 若無武俊，欲使誰為大夫卻敵乎！」

translations.literal: Without Wujun, whom do you want to turn the enemy back for you, Lord!
translations.idiomatic: Without Wujun, who will fight the enemy back for you?"

sentences.zh: 惟岳以為然，乃使步軍使衛常寧與武俊共擊趙州，又使王士真將兵宿府中以自衛。

translations.literal: Weiyue thought this right, sent infantry commander Wei Changning with Wujun jointly to strike Zhaozhou, and also had Wang Shizhen camp troops in the headquarters compound for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue agreed, sent the infantry commander Wei Changning with Wujun to attack Zhaozhou, and posted Wang Shizhen with troops in the headquarters compound as a guard.

sentences.zh: 癸未，蜀王遂更名溯。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Prince of Shu changed his name to Su.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day, the Prince of Shu changed his name to Su.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少游拔海、密二州，李納復攻陷之。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou, military commissioner of Huainan, recovered Hai and Mi prefectures; Li Na attacked and took them again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou, military commissioner of Huainan, recovered Hai and Mi; Li Na attacked and seized them again.

sentences.zh: 王武俊既出恆州，謂衛常寧曰：「武俊今幸出虎口，不復歸矣！

translations.literal: Wang Wujun having left Hengzhou, said to Wei Changning: "Wujun has luckily escaped the tiger's maw and will not return!
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Wujun was out of Hengzhou, he told Wei Changning, "I have escaped the tiger's jaws and will not go back!

sentences.zh: 當北歸張尚書。」

translations.literal: I ought to go north to Senior Minister Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: I should march north to Senior Minister Zhang."

sentences.zh: 常寧曰：「大夫闇弱，信任左右，觀其勢終為朱滔所滅。

translations.literal: Changning said: "The Lord is dim and weak, trusts those at his side; judging the trend he will in the end be destroyed by Zhu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Changning said, "The Lord is weak and trusts his flatterers; in the end Zhu Tao will destroy him.

sentences.zh: 今天子有詔，得大夫首者，以其官爵與之。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven has an edict: whoever obtains the Lord's head receives his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has promised the Lord's rank and office to whoever brings in his head.

sentences.zh: 中丞素為眾所服，與其出亡，曷若倒戈以取大夫，轉禍為福，特反掌耳。

translations.literal: You, Commissioner, have long won the troops' respect; rather than flee abroad, why not turn your weapons and seize the Lord—turn disaster to fortune, no harder than turning your palm.
translations.idiomatic: You, Commissioner, have long commanded the troops' respect. Rather than flee, why not turn your blades on the Lord and trade ruin for reward—it is no harder than turning your hand over.

sentences.zh: 事苟不捷，歸張尚書，未晚也。」

translations.literal: If the affair fails, going to Senior Minister Zhang is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: If the plan fails, you can still go to Zhang—it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 武俊深以為然。

translations.literal: Wujun deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was fully persuaded.

sentences.zh: 會惟岳使要藉謝遵至趙州城下，武俊引遵同謀取惟岳。

translations.literal: It happened that Weiyue sent Yaoji Xie Zun to the walls of Zhaozhou; Wujun drew Zun into plotting to seize Weiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue's supply officer Xie Zun came to the walls of Zhaozhou; Wujun drew him into a plot to seize Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 遵還，密告王士真。

translations.literal: Zun returned and secretly told Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zun returned and secretly informed Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 閏月，甲辰，武俊、常寧自趙州引兵還襲惟岳。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiachen, Wujun and Changning led troops back from Zhaozhou to strike Weiyue by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the jiachen day, Wujun and Changning marched back from Zhaozhou and struck at Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 遵與士真矯惟岳命，啟城門納之。
