translations.literal: Zun and Shizhen forged Weiyue's order and opened the gate to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Zun and Shizhen forged an order in Weiyue's name and opened the gates to let them in.

sentences.zh: 黎明，武俊帥數百騎突入府門。

translations.literal: At dawn Wujun led several hundred horsemen in a sudden rush through the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Wujun led several hundred horsemen in a sudden charge through the headquarters gate.

sentences.zh: 士真應之於內，殺十餘人。

translations.literal: Shizhen answered from within and killed more than ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen answered from within and cut down more than ten men.

sentences.zh: 武俊令曰：「大夫叛逆，將士歸順，敢違拒者族！」

translations.literal: Wujun proclaimed: "The Lord has rebelled; soldiers obey the throne—whoever dares resist will have his clan exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun proclaimed, "The Lord has rebelled; the troops are to submit to the throne. Whoever resists will have his clan wiped out!"

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢動。

translations.literal: No one dared move.
translations.idiomatic: No one stirred.

sentences.zh: 遂執惟岳，收鄭詵、畢華、王它奴等，皆殺之。

translations.literal: They seized Weiyue, arrested Zheng Shen, Bi Hua, Wang Tanu, and others, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Weiyue, arrested Zheng Shen, Bi Hua, Wang Tanu, and the rest, and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 武俊以惟岳舊使之子，欲生送之長安。

translations.literal: Wujun, because Weiyue had been a son he once served, wished to send him alive to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun, remembering that Weiyue had been the son of his old master, wished to deliver him alive to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 常寧曰：「彼見天子，將復以叛逆之罪歸咎於中丞。」

translations.literal: Changning said: "When he sees the Son of Heaven he will again lay the crime of rebellion on you, Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Changning said, "Once he sees the Son of Heaven he will lay the whole rebellion at your door again."

sentences.zh: 乃縊殺之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: They strangled him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: So they garroted him and forwarded his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 深州刺史楊榮國，惟岳姊夫也，降於朱滔，滔使復其位。

translations.literal: Yang Rongguo, prefect of Shenzhou and Weiyue's brother-in-law, surrendered to Zhu Tao; Tao had him restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rongguo, prefect of Shenzhou and Weiyue's brother-in-law, submitted to Zhu Tao, who restored him to his post.

sentences.zh: 復榷天下酒，惟西京不榷。

translations.literal: Wine monopolies were restored throughout the realm, except in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored the wine monopoly empire-wide, exempting only the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊午，李惟岳所署定州刺史楊政義降。

translations.literal: Second month, wuwu day, Yang Zhengyi, prefect of Dingzhou appointed by Li Weiyue, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the wuwu day, Yang Zhengyi, the Dingzhou prefect Li Weiyue had appointed, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時河北略定，惟魏州未下。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei was largely pacified; only Weizhou was not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hebei was largely pacified; only Weizhou still held out.

sentences.zh: 河南諸軍攻李納於濮州，納勢日蹙。

translations.literal: The Henan armies attacked Li Na at Puzhou; Na's position grew daily tighter.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan armies pressed Li Na at Puzhou, and his position grew tighter by the day.

sentences.zh: 朝廷謂天下不日可平。

translations.literal: The court believed the realm would be pacified within days.
translations.idiomatic: At court men spoke as though the empire would be at peace in a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以張孝忠為易、定、滄三州節度使，王武俊為恆冀都團練觀察使，康日知為深趙都團練觀察使，以德、林二州隸朱滔，令還鎮。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhang Xiaozhong was made military commissioner of Yi, Ding, and Cang; Wang Wujun made regimental-training and observation commissioner of Heng and Ji; Kang Rizhi of Shen and Zhao; De and Lin prefectures were placed under Zhu Tao with orders to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, Zhang Xiaozhong was made military commissioner of Yi, Ding, and Cang; Wang Wujun regimental-training commissioner of Heng and Ji; Kang Rizhi of Shen and Zhao; De and Lin were assigned to Zhu Tao, who was ordered back to his command.

sentences.zh: 滔固請深州，不許，由是怨望，留屯深州。

translations.literal: Tao pressed hard for Shenzhou and was refused; hence resentment, and he remained encamped at Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao pressed for Shenzhou and was refused; resentful, he kept his army at Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 王武俊素輕張孝忠，自以手誅李惟岳，功在康日知上，而孝忠為節度使，己與康日知俱為都團練使，又失趙、定二州，亦不悅。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun had always looked down on Zhang Xiaozhong; he felt he had personally killed Li Weiyue, his merit above Kang Rizhi's, yet Xiaozhong became military commissioner while he and Kang Rizhi were only regimental-training commissioners, and he had lost Zhao and Ding besides—he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun had always despised Zhang Xiaozhong; he had killed Li Weiyue with his own hand and outranked Kang Rizhi in merit, yet Xiaozhong received a full commission while he and Kang Rizhi were only regimental-training commissioners—and he had lost Zhao and Ding besides. He was bitter.

sentences.zh: 又詔以糧三千石給朱滔，馬五百匹給馬燧。

translations.literal: An edict also gave Zhu Tao three thousand piculs of grain and Ma Sui five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict assigned three thousand piculs of grain to Zhu Tao and five hundred horses to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 武俊以為朝廷不欲使故人為節度使，魏博既下，必取恆冀，故先分其糧馬以弱之，疑，未肯奉詔。

translations.literal: Wujun thought the court did not want an old subordinate as commissioner; once Weibo fell Heng and Ji would surely be taken, so grain and horses were divided off first to weaken him—suspicious, he would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun concluded that the court would not let an old retainer hold a full commission: once Weibo fell, Heng and Ji would be next, and the grain and horses were being stripped away in advance to weaken him. Suspicious, he refused the order.

sentences.zh: 田悅聞之，遣判官王侑、許士則間道至深州，說朱滔曰：「司徒奉詔討李惟岳，旬朔之間，拔束鹿，下深州，惟岳勢蹙，故王大夫因司徒勝勢，得以梟惟岳之首，此皆司徒之功也。

translations.literal: Tian Yue heard, sent recorders Wang You and Xu Shize by secret route to Shenzhou, and said to Zhu Tao: "Steward, you received orders to attack Li Weiyue; within a month and a half you took Shulu, reduced Shenzhou, Weiyue's force was cornered, so Lord Wang the physician used your victorious momentum to take Weiyue's head—all this is your achievement, Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yue heard, he sent his recorders Wang You and Xu Shize by a hidden route to Shenzhou to tell Zhu Tao, "Steward, you were ordered to attack Li Weiyue. Within a month you took Shulu and Shenzhou; Weiyue was cornered, and Lord Wang used your victory to take Weiyue's head—all of it your doing, Steward.

sentences.zh: 又天子明下詔書，令司徒得惟岳城邑，皆隸本鎮。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven clearly issued edicts that cities you, Steward, took from Weiyue all belong to your original command.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven plainly decreed that every city you took from Weiyue should remain under your command.

sentences.zh: 今乃割深州以與日知，是自棄其信也。

translations.literal: Now Shenzhou is carved off and given to Rizhi—this is throwing away your own credibility.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shenzhou is handed to Kang Rizhi—you are throwing away your own credibility.

sentences.zh: 且今上志欲掃清河朔，不使蕃鎮承襲，將悉以文臣代武臣。

translations.literal: Moreover the present emperor intends to sweep Qinghe and Heshuo clean, not allow frontier commands to pass in succession, and will replace military men entirely with civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the present emperor means to sweep Qinghe and the north clean, end hereditary frontier commands, and replace every military commissioner with a civil official.

sentences.zh: 魏亡，則燕、趙為之次矣；

translations.literal: If Wei perishes, Yan and Zhao are next;
translations.idiomatic: If Wei falls, Yan and Zhao are next;

sentences.zh: 若魏存，則燕、趙無患。

translations.literal: if Wei survives, Yan and Zhao have no worry.
translations.idiomatic: if Wei survives, Yan and Zhao have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 然則司徒果有意矜魏博之危而救之，非徒得存亡繼絕之義，亦子孫萬世之利也。」

translations.literal: Thus if you, Steward, truly mean to pity Weibo in peril and save it, you gain not only the righteousness of preserving what was dying, but profit for your descendants for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If you, Steward, truly mean to pity Weibo in its peril and save it, you win not only the credit of preserving the dying, but profit for your house for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 又許以貝州賂滔。

translations.literal: They also promised Beizhou as a bribe to Tao.
translations.idiomatic: They also offered Beizhou as a bribe to Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 滔素有異志，聞之，大喜，即遣王侑歸報魏州，使將士知有外援，各自堅。

translations.literal: Tao had long harbored a separate design; hearing this he was greatly pleased, immediately sent Wang You back to report to Weizhou so troops would know outside aid existed and each grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao had long nursed ambitions of his own; delighted, he sent Wang You back to Weizhou so the garrison would know outside aid was coming and stand firmer.

sentences.zh: 又遣判官王郅與許士則俱詣恆州，說王武俊曰：「大夫出萬死之計，誅逆首，拔亂根，康日知不出趙州，豈得與大夫同日論功！

translations.literal: He also sent recorder Wang Zhi with Xu Shize together to Hengzhou to persuade Wang Wujun: "Lord, you risked death's ten thousand paths, slew the rebel leader, uprooted disorder's root—Kang Rizhi never left Zhaozhou, how could he be discussed in the same breath for merit!
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Wang Zhi and Xu Shize to Hengzhou to persuade Wang Wujun: "Lord, you risked death ten thousand times over, slew the rebel leader, and uprooted the rebellion—Kang Rizhi never left Zhaozhou; how can he be ranked with you for merit!

sentences.zh: 而朝廷褒賞略同，誰不為大夫憤邑者！

translations.literal: Yet court rewards are nearly the same—who does not seethe on your behalf, Lord!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court's rewards are nearly the same—who does not burn with outrage on your behalf!

sentences.zh: 今又聞有詔支糧馬與鄰道，朝廷之意，蓋以大夫善戰無敵，恐為後患，先欲貧弱軍府，俟平魏之日，使馬僕射北首，朱司徒南向，共相滅耳。

translations.literal: Now we hear an edict assigning grain and horses to neighboring circuits—the court's intent is surely that you, Lord, fight beyond compare and they fear future trouble; they wish first to impoverish your military prefecture, and when Wei is pacified have Vice Minister Ma face north and Steward Zhu face south to destroy each other.
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear an edict diverting your grain and horses to neighboring circuits. The court fears you are invincible in battle and means to weaken your prefecture first; when Wei is pacified, Vice Minister Ma will march north and Steward Zhu south to destroy each other—and you with them.

sentences.zh: 朱司徒亦不敢自保，使郅等效愚計，欲與大夫共救田尚書而存之。

translations.literal: Steward Zhu also dares not trust his own safety; he sent Zhi and others with this foolish plan, wishing with you, Lord, jointly to rescue Senior Minister Tian and preserve him.
translations.idiomatic: Steward Zhu dares not trust his own safety either; he sent Zhi with this plan, hoping with you to rescue Senior Minister Tian and keep him alive.

sentences.zh: 大夫自留糧馬以供軍；

translations.literal: You, Lord, keep the grain and horses for your army;
translations.idiomatic: Keep the grain and horses for your own army;

sentences.zh: 朱司徒不欲以深州與康日知，願以與大夫，請早定刺史以守之。

translations.literal: Steward Zhu does not wish to give Shenzhou to Kang Rizhi but to you, Lord—please soon appoint a prefect to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Steward Zhu will not give Shenzhou to Kang Rizhi but to you—appoint a prefect at once to hold it.

sentences.zh: 三鎮連後，若耳目手足之相救，則它日永無患矣！」

translations.literal: With the three commands linked behind one another like ear, eye, hand, and foot aiding each other, thereafter there will never be trouble!
translations.idiomatic: With the three commands linked like ear, eye, hand, and foot, you will never have trouble again!"

sentences.zh: 武俊亦喜，許諾，即遣判官王巨源使於滔，且令知深州事，相與刻日舉兵南向。

translations.literal: Wujun too was pleased, promised, immediately sent recorder Wang Juyuan to Tao and put him in charge of Shenzhou affairs, setting a day together to raise troops southward.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was pleased in turn, agreed, and at once sent Wang Juyuan to Zhu Tao, put him in charge of Shenzhou, and set a day to march south together.

sentences.zh: 滔又遣人說張孝忠，孝忠不從。

translations.literal: Tao also sent men to persuade Zhang Xiaozhong; Xiaozhong would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao also sent envoys to win over Zhang Xiaozhong, but Xiaozhong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使劉洽攻李納於濮州，克其外城。

translations.literal: Liu Qia, military commissioner of Xuanwu, attacked Li Na at Puzhou and took the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia, military commissioner of Xuanwu, besieged Li Na at Puzhou and took the outer city.

sentences.zh: 納於城上涕泣求自新，李勉又遣人說之。

translations.literal: Na on the wall wept and begged to reform; Li Mian also sent men to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na wept on the walls and begged to reform; Li Mian also sent envoys to urge him.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，納遣其判官房說以其母弟經及子成務入見。

translations.literal: On guimao, Na sent his recorder Fang Shuo with his mother-born younger brother Jing and son Chengwu to audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, Li Na sent his recorder Fang Shuo with his younger brother Jing and his son Chengwu to court.

sentences.zh: 會中使宋鳳朝稱納勢窮蹙，不可捨，上乃因說等於禁中，納遂歸鄆州，復與田悅等合。

translations.literal: At that time the palace envoy Song Fengchao said Na's force was exhausted and cornered and must not be let go; the emperor therefore detained Shuo and the rest in the palace precincts; Na then returned to Yanzhou and again joined Tian Yue and others.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy Song Fengchao declared that Li Na was cornered and must not be spared; the emperor detained Fang Shuo and the rest in the palace, and Na returned to Yanzhou and rejoined Tian Yue and the others.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以納勢未衰，三月，乙未，始以徐州刺史李洧兼徐、海、沂都團練觀察使，海、沂已為納所據，洧競無所得。

translations.literal: The court, because Na's strength had not yet waned, in the third month on yiwei first appointed Li Wei, prefect of Xuzhou, also regimental-training commissioner of Xu, Hai, and Yi—but Hai and Yi were already held by Na, and Wei gained nothing in the struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Na's strength had not yet broken, in the third month on the yiwei day the court first named Li Wei of Xuzhou regimental-training commissioner of Xu, Hai, and Yi as well—but Hai and Yi were already in Na's hands, and Wei gained nothing for the title.

sentences.zh: 李納之初反也，其所署德州刺史李西華備守甚嚴，都虞候李士真密毀西華於納，納召西華還府，以士真代之。

translations.literal: When Li Na first rebelled, his appointed Dezhou prefect Li Xihua guarded very strictly; chief marshal Li Shizhen secretly slandered Xihua to Na; Na summoned Xihua back to headquarters and replaced him with Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na first rebelled, his Dezhou prefect Li Xihua held the city with strict discipline; the chief marshal Li Shizhen secretly slandered him to Na, who recalled Xihua to headquarters and replaced him with Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 士真又以詐召棣州刺史李長卿，長卿過德州，士真劫之，與同歸國。

translations.literal: Shizhen also by fraud summoned Di prefect Li Changqing; Changqing passed through Dezhou and Shizhen seized him and together they returned to imperial allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen also lured Di prefect Li Changqing by fraud; when Changqing passed through Dezhou, Shizhen seized him and they submitted together to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊午，以士真、長卿為二州刺史。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, wuwu, Shizhen and Changqing were made the two prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the wuwu day, Shizhen and Changqing were confirmed as the two prefects.

sentences.zh: 士真求援於朱滔，滔已有異志，遣大將李濟時將三千人聲言助士真守德州，且召士真詣深州議軍事，至則留之，使濟時領州事。

translations.literal: Shizhen sought aid from Zhu Tao; Tao already had a separate design, sent great general Li Jishi with three thousand men claiming to help Shizhen hold Dezhou, and also summoned Shizhen to Shenzhou to discuss military affairs; on arrival he detained him and had Jishi administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen sought aid from Zhu Tao, who already nursed separate ambitions; he sent Li Jishi with three thousand men, claiming to help hold Dezhou, summoned Shizhen to Shenzhou to discuss strategy, detained him on arrival, and put Jishi in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚申，吐蕃歸曏日所俘掠兵民八百人。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Tibet returned eight hundred soldiers and civilians captured on a recent day.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day, Tibet returned eight hundred soldiers and civilians taken in a recent raid.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使發盧龍、恆冀、易定兵萬人詣魏州討田悅。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to mobilize ten thousand troops from Lulong, Heng-Ji, and Yi-Ding to march on Weizhou against Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to raise ten thousand men from Lulong, Heng-Ji, and Yi-Ding and march on Weizhou against Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 王武俊不受詔，執使者送朱滔。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun refused the edict, seized the envoy and sent him to Zhu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun refused the order, seized the envoy, and handed him over to Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 滔言於眾曰：「將士有功者，吾奏求官勳，皆不遂。

translations.literal: Tao said to the multitude: "Soldiers and officers with achievement—I have memorialized requesting offices and merit rewards, and none have been granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao told the troops, "Every officer and soldier with merit—I have petitioned for rank and rewards, and not one has been granted.

sentences.zh: 今欲與諸君敕裝共趨魏州，擊破馬燧以取溫飽，何如？」

translations.literal: Now I wish together with you gentlemen to don gear and together hurry to Weizhou, smash Ma Sui to obtain warm clothing and full bellies—how about it?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean for all of you to arm up and march with me on Weizhou, break Ma Sui, and win ourselves food and warm clothes—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 皆不應。

translations.literal: None answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 三問，乃曰：「幽州之人，自安、史之反，從而南者無一人得還，今其遺人痛入骨髓。

translations.literal: After three questions, they then said: "Men of Youzhou—since the An-Shi rebellion, of those who followed southward not one has been able to return; those who remain now feel pain penetrating to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: He asked three times before they spoke: "Since the An Lushan rebellion, every Youzhou man who marched south has failed to come home. Those left behind carry that grief in their bones.

sentences.zh: 況太尉、司徒皆受國寵榮，將士亦各蒙官勳，誠且願保目前，不敢復有僥冀。」

translations.literal: Moreover the Grand Preceptor and Situ have both received the state's favor and glory; officers and soldiers too have each received rank and merit awards—we truly wish only to preserve the present and dare not again harbor wild hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you and the Situ already enjoy the court's highest honors, and we have our own ranks and rewards. We mean to hold what we have and dare not gamble for more."

sentences.zh: 滔默然而罷。

translations.literal: Tao fell silent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tao said nothing more and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 乃誅大將數十人，厚撫循其士卒。

translations.literal: He then executed several dozen great generals and generously comforted and rallied his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He executed several dozen senior commanders, then lavished care on the ranks to steady them.

sentences.zh: 康日知聞其謀，以告馬燧，燧以聞。

translations.literal: Kang Rizhi heard of the plot and reported it to Ma Sui; Sui reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Rizhi learned of the scheme, told Ma Sui, and Sui reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以魏州未下，王武俊復叛，力未能制滔。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Weizhou had not yet fallen and Wang Wujun had rebelled again, lacked strength to control Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou still held out, Wang Wujun had turned rebel again, and the court lacked the strength to bring Zhu Tao to heel.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，賜滔爵通義郡王，冀以安之。

translations.literal: On renxu, Tao was granted the title Prince of Tongyi Commandery, hoping thereby to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day the throne made Tao Prince of Tongyi, hoping the honor would keep him loyal.

sentences.zh: 滔反謀益甚，分兵營於趙州以逼康日知，以深州授王巨源。

translations.literal: Tao's rebellious plotting grew ever worse; he divided troops to encamp at Zhaozhou to pressure Kang Rizhi and gave Shenzhou to Wang Juyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's defiance only deepened. He posted troops at Zhaozhou to squeeze Kang Rizhi and handed Shenzhou to Wang Juyuan.

sentences.zh: 武俊以其子士真為恆、冀、深三州留後，將兵圍趙州。

translations.literal: Wujun made his son Shizhen acting governor of the three prefectures Heng, Ji, and Shen and led troops to besiege Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun installed his son Shizhen as acting governor of Heng, Ji, and Shen, then marched to besiege Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 涿州刺史劉怦與滔同縣人，其母，滔之姑也，滔使知幽州留後，聞滔欲救田悅，以書諫之曰：「今昌平故里，朝廷改為太尉鄉、司徒裡，此亦大夫不朽之名也。

translations.literal: Zhuo Prefecture prefect Liu Zheng was a fellow townsman of Tao's; his mother was Tao's paternal aunt. Tao had appointed him acting Youzhou governor. Hearing Tao wished to rescue Tian Yue, he remonstrated by letter: "Your native Changping— the court has renamed it Grand Preceptor Village and Situ Lane. This too is an immortal name for you, Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng of Zhuo prefecture came from Tao's home county; his mother was Tao's aunt. Tao had left him in charge at Youzhou. When he heard Tao meant to march south for Tian Yue, he wrote in protest: "The court has renamed your old home at Changping Grand Preceptor Village and Situ Lane—that is glory enough for any man.

sentences.zh: 但以忠順自持，則事無不濟。

translations.literal: Only hold fast to loyalty and obedience, and nothing will fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Hold to loyalty and obedience, and every undertaking will prosper.

sentences.zh: 竊思近日務大樂戰，不顧成敗而家滅身屠者，安、史是也。

translations.literal: I reflect privately that those in recent days who pursued grand designs and delighted in battle, heedless of success or failure until house destroyed and body slaughtered—were An and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: I think of men who lately chased grand ambitions and loved battle, never weighing victory or ruin until their houses were destroyed and they themselves were slain—An Lushan and Shi Siming were such men.

sentences.zh: 怦忝密親，默而無告，是負重知。

translations.literal: Zheng, though honored with close kinship, were I silent and not to inform, would be failing your deep trust.
translations.idiomatic: As one bound to you by close kin, I would betray your trust were I to keep silent.

sentences.zh: 惟司徒圖之，無貽後悔。」

translations.literal: I pray only that the Situ consider this and leave no cause for regret."
translations.idiomatic: Please weigh this, Situ, and spare yourself regret."

sentences.zh: 滔雖不用其言，亦嘉其盡忠，卒無疑貳。

translations.literal: Though Tao did not use his words, he also praised his full loyalty and in the end harbored no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao ignored the advice but honored his loyalty and never doubted him afterward.

sentences.zh: 滔將起兵，恐張孝忠為後患，復遣牙官蔡雄往說之。

translations.literal: As Tao was about to raise troops, fearing Zhang Xiaozhong as a rear trouble, he again sent aide Cai Xiong to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tao took the field he feared Zhang Xiaozhong might strike from behind and sent his aide Cai Xiong to win him over.

sentences.zh: 孝忠曰：「昔者司徒發幽州，遣人語孝忠曰：『李惟岳負恩為逆』，謂孝忠歸國即為忠臣。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong said: "Long ago when the Situ marched from Youzhou, he sent someone telling Xiaozhong: 'Li Weiyue betrayed grace and turned rebel,' saying that if Xiaozhong returned to the state he would be a loyal subject.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong replied: "When you first marched from Youzhou you told me Li Weiyue had betrayed the throne and that if I returned to the empire I would be counted loyal.

sentences.zh: 孝忠性直，用司徒之教。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong is straightforward by nature and followed the Situ's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: I am a plain man and took your counsel.

sentences.zh: 今既為忠臣矣，不復助逆也。

translations.literal: Now I am already a loyal subject and will not again aid rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: I am already the emperor's man and will not aid rebellion again.

sentences.zh: 且孝忠與武俊皆出夷落，深知其心最喜翻覆。

translations.literal: Moreover Xiaozhong and Wujun both come from frontier tribes; I know well their hearts most love to turn and reverse.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun and I both come from the frontier tribes—I know how fond he is of changing sides.

sentences.zh: 司徒勿忘鄙言，它日必相念矣！」

translations.literal: Situ, do not forget my humble words—you will surely recall them another day!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not forget what I tell you now, Situ—you will remember it one day!"

sentences.zh: 雄復欲以巧辭說之，孝忠怒，欲執送京師。

translations.literal: Xiong again wished to persuade him with clever words; Xiaozhong grew angry and wished to seize and send him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong tried more smooth talk, Xiaozhong flew into a rage and meant to seize him and send him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 雄懼，逃歸。

translations.literal: Xiong, afraid, fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 滔乃使劉怦將兵屯要害以備之。

translations.literal: Tao then had Liu Zheng lead troops to garrison strategic points against him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao posted Liu Zheng with troops at the key passes to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 孝忠完城礪兵，獨居強寇之間，莫之能屈。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong repaired walls and sharpened arms, standing alone among mighty foes; none could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong repaired his walls, trained his men, and held his ground amid powerful enemies—none could break him.

sentences.zh: 滔將步騎二萬五千發深州，至束鹿。

translations.literal: Tao led twenty-five thousand foot and horse from Shenzhou and reached Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao marched twenty-five thousand infantry and cavalry from Shenzhou as far as Shulu.

sentences.zh: 詰旦將行，吹角未畢，士卒忽大亂，喧噪曰：「天子令司徒歸幽州，奈何違敕南救田悅！」

translations.literal: At dawn as he was about to march, before the horn call finished, the soldiers suddenly erupted in great disorder, shouting: "The Son of Heaven ordered the Situ back to Youzhou—why defy the edict and march south to rescue Tian Yue!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, before the reveille had finished, the troops erupted in uproar: "The Son of Heaven ordered the Situ home to Youzhou—why disobey and march south for Tian Yue!"

sentences.zh: 滔大懼，走入驛後堂避匿。

translations.literal: Tao was greatly afraid and fled into the relay station's rear hall to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was terrified and hid in the back hall of the post station.

sentences.zh: 蔡雄與兵馬使宗頊等矯謂士卒曰：「汝輩勿喧，聽司徒傳令。」

translations.literal: Cai Xiong and troop commander Zong Xu and others falsely announced to the soldiers: "Do not clamor—listen for the Situ to transmit his order."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiong and the troop commander Zong Xu stepped in with a false announcement: "Quiet—all of you. Hear the Situ's order."

sentences.zh: 眾稍止。

translations.literal: The crowd gradually quieted.
translations.idiomatic: The uproar subsided a little.

sentences.zh: 雄又曰：「司徒將發范陽，恩旨令得李惟岳州縣即有之，司徒以幽州少絲纊，故與汝曹竭力血戰以取深州，冀得其絲纊以寬汝曹賦率，不意國家無信，復以深州與康日知。

translations.literal: Xiong said again: "When the Situ was about to depart Fan Yang, a grace edict said Li Weiyue's prefectures and counties would now be his. Because Youzhou lacks silk and hemp, he fought alongside you with all blood to take Shenzhou, hoping to obtain its silk and hemp to ease your tax burdens—who expected the state to break faith and give Shenzhou again to Kang Rizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong went on: "When we left Fan Yang the throne promised us Li Weiyue's districts. Youzhou lacks cloth, so the Situ bled beside you to seize Shenzhou so its hemp and silk could lighten your taxes. Then the court broke faith and handed Shenzhou back to Kang Rizhi.

sentences.zh: 又，朝廷以汝曹有功，賜絹人十匹，至魏州西境，盡為馬僕射所奪。

translations.literal: Further, because you had merit the court granted each man ten bolts of silk; at Weizhou's western border all were seized by Vice Censor-in-Chief Ma.
translations.idiomatic: The court also granted each of you ten bolts of silk for your service, but at the western border of Weizhou Vice Censor Ma seized every bolt.

sentences.zh: 司徒但處范陽，富貴足矣，今茲南行，乃為汝曹，非自為也。

translations.literal: The Situ need only remain at Fan Yang and wealth and honor suffice; this march south is for you, not for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Situ could live in wealth at Fan Yang. He marches south for you, not for himself.

sentences.zh: 汝曹不欲南行，任自歸北，何用喧悖，乖失軍禮！」

translations.literal: If you do not wish to march south, go back north as you please—why make uproar and violate military discipline!"
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to march south, go north on your own—but why riot and break discipline?"

sentences.zh: 眾聞言，不知所為，乃曰：「敕使何得不為軍士守護賞物！」

translations.literal: Hearing this, the crowd did not know what to do and said: "Why did the edict envoy not guard the reward goods for the soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: The men were at a loss, then cried: "Why didn't the imperial envoy protect our reward goods!"

sentences.zh: 遂入敕使院，擘裂殺之。

translations.literal: They then entered the edict envoy's compound, tore him apart, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the envoy's quarters, tore him limb from limb, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 又呼曰：「雖知司徒此行為士卒，終不如且奉詔歸鎮。」

translations.literal: They cried again: "Though we know this march is for the soldiers, we had still better obey the edict and return to our garrison."
translations.idiomatic: They shouted again: "Even if this march is for us, we had better obey the edict and go home to our posts."

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「然則汝曹各還部伍，詰朝復往深州，休息數日，相與歸鎮耳。」

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Then each of you return to your ranks; tomorrow we shall again proceed to Shenzhou, rest several days, and together return to our garrison."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong said: "Fall back into your units. Tomorrow we march again to Shenzhou, rest a few days, then all return to our posts together."

sentences.zh: 眾然後定。

translations.literal: The crowd then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the troops calm down.

sentences.zh: 滔即引軍還深州，密令諸將訪察唱率為亂者，得二百餘人，悉斬之，餘眾股慄。

translations.literal: Tao at once led the army back to Shenzhou and secretly ordered his generals to investigate those who led the riot; over two hundred were found and all beheaded; the rest trembled in their thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Tao withdrew to Shenzhou and secretly had his officers find the ringleaders—more than two hundred were beheaded, and the rest shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 乃復舉兵而南，眾莫敢前卻。

translations.literal: He then again raised troops and marched south; none dared advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south again, and no soldier dared hang back or press ahead on his own.

sentences.zh: 進，取寧晉，留屯以待王武俊。

translations.literal: Advancing, he took Ningjin and encamped to await Wang Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, seized Ningjin, and camped there to await Wang Wujun.

sentences.zh: 武俊將步騎萬五千取元氏，東趣寧晉。

translations.literal: Wujun led fifteen thousand foot and horse to take Yuanshi and pressed east toward Ningjin.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun led fifteen thousand foot and horse to take Yuanshi and hurried east toward Ningjin.

sentences.zh: 武俊之始誅李惟岳也，遣判官孟華入見。

translations.literal: When Wujun first killed Li Weiyue, he sent his registrar Meng Hua to have an audience.
translations.idiomatic: After Wujun killed Li Weiyue he sent his registrar Meng Hua to court.

sentences.zh: 上問以河朔利害，華性忠直，有才略，應對慷慨。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the advantages and perils of the Hebei region; Hua was loyal and upright by nature, possessed talent and stratagem, and answered boldly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him on the strategic situation north of the Yellow River. Loyal, capable, and forthright, Hua answered with force and clarity.

sentences.zh: 上悅，以為恆冀團練副使。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and appointed him deputy commissioner for Heng-Ji training and defense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and made him deputy commissioner for Heng and Ji.

sentences.zh: 會武俊與朱滔有異謀，上遽遣華歸諭旨。

translations.literal: Just then Wujun and Zhu Tao had separate schemes; the emperor hastily sent Hua back to announce the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wujun and Zhu Tao began to plot separately, the emperor hurried Hua back to deliver the court's message.

sentences.zh: 華至，武俊已出師，華諫曰：「聖意於大夫甚厚，苟盡忠義，何患官爵之不崇，土地之不廣，不日天子必移康中丞於它鎮，深、趙終為大夫之有，何苦遽自同於逆亂乎！

translations.literal: Hua arrived after Wujun had already taken the field. Hua remonstrated: "His Majesty's favor toward you, Grandee, is very deep. If you uphold loyalty and righteousness, what worry that rank will not rise or territory broaden? Before long the Son of Heaven will surely move Assistant Commissioner Kang elsewhere; Shen and Zhao will in the end be yours—why rush to join rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Hua arrived to find Wujun already on campaign. He pleaded: "The throne favors you deeply. Serve with loyalty and rank and lands will follow. Kang will soon be transferred; Shen and Zhao will be yours in time. Why throw in with rebels now?

sentences.zh: 異日無成，悔之何及！」

translations.literal: If another day you fail, how will regret reach you!"
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, regret will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 華曏在李寶臣幕府，以直道已為同列所忌，至是為副使，同列尤疾之，言於武俊曰：「華以軍中陰事奏天子，請為內應，故得超遷。

translations.literal: Hua had formerly been in Li Baochen's staff; for his upright conduct his colleagues already resented him. Now as deputy commissioner his colleagues hated him all the more and said to Wujun: "Hua reported the army's secret affairs to the Son of Heaven and asked to serve as an insider, and so won sudden promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had once served Li Baochen and his honesty had already earned jealousy. As deputy commissioner the staff hated him worse and told Wujun: "He reported our secrets to the emperor and offered to be his spy inside the army—that is why he was promoted so fast.

sentences.zh: 是將覆大夫之軍，大夫宜備之。」

translations.literal: He means to overturn the Grandee's army—the Grandee should guard against him."
translations.idiomatic: He means to destroy your army, my lord—you should guard against him."

sentences.zh: 武俊以其舊人，不忍殺，奪職，使歸私第。

translations.literal: Wujun, because he was an old associate, could not bear to kill him; he stripped him of office and sent him to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun, remembering their old tie, would not kill him but stripped his post and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 田悅恃援兵將至，遣其將康愔萬餘人出城西，與馬燧等戰於御河上，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Tian Yue, relying on relief troops about to arrive, sent his general Kang Yin with more than ten thousand men out west of the city to fight Ma Sui and others on the Yu River; they were routed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Counting on reinforcements, Tian Yue sent Kang Yin with ten thousand men west of the city to meet Ma Sui on the Yu River. They were crushed and driven back.

sentences.zh: 時兩河用兵，月費百餘萬緡，府庫不支數月。

translations.literal: At this time the two Hebei campaigns cost more than a million strings of cash per month; the treasury could not sustain several months.
translations.idiomatic: The two Hebei fronts now cost more than a million strings a month, and the treasury could not last many months.

sentences.zh: 太常博士韋都賓、陳京建議，以為：「貨利所聚，皆在富商，請括富商錢，出萬緡者，借其餘以供軍。

translations.literal: Grand Academy doctors Wei Dubin and Chen Jing proposed: "Where profit and goods gather is entirely among great merchants. We ask to survey wealthy merchants' funds—those contributing ten thousand strings would lend the remainder to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academy doctors Wei Dubin and Chen Jing urged: "Wealth pools among the great merchants. Register their assets—let each man who holds ten thousand strings lend the rest to the army.

sentences.zh: 計天下不過借一二千商，則數年之用足矣。」

translations.literal: Calculating for the realm, borrowing from no more than one or two thousand merchants would suffice for several years' expenses."
translations.idiomatic: A loan from one or two thousand merchants across the empire would fund the war for years."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔借商人錢，令度支條上。

translations.literal: On jiazi, an edict ordered borrowing merchants' funds and directed the Revenue Bureau to submit itemized plans.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day an edict ordered loans from merchants and told the Revenue Bureau to draw up the lists.

sentences.zh: 判度支杜佑大索長安中商賈所有貨，意其不實，輒加搒捶。

translations.literal: Revenue Vice Minister Du You greatly searched out all goods held by merchants in Chang'an; when he deemed declarations untrue he at once added cudgel blows.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Vice Minister Du You scoured Chang'an for merchant goods and beat any man he thought had lied about his holdings.

sentences.zh: 帛粟麥者，皆借四分之一，封其櫃窖。

translations.literal: For cloth, grain, and wheat, a quarter of each was borrowed and their chests and cellars sealed.
translations.idiomatic: A quarter of every stock of cloth, grain, and wheat was seized and the storerooms sealed.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之罷市，相帥遮宰相馬自訴，以千萬數。

translations.literal: The people for this shut the markets; they led one another to block the chief ministers' horses and plead, in groups of thousands upon thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The people shut the markets in protest and massed by the thousands to block the chief ministers' carriages and plead their case.

sentences.zh: 盧杞始慰諭之，勢不可遏，乃疾驅自他道歸。

translations.literal: Lu Qi at first soothed and instructed them, but the momentum could not be stopped; he then whipped his horse down another road home.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi tried to calm them, but the crowd could not be checked, so he galloped home by a back street.

sentences.zh: 計並借商所得，才二百萬緡，人已竭矣。

translations.literal: Counting all borrowed from merchants together, it came to only two million strings—and the people were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the levy raised only two million strings, while the people were drained dry.

sentences.zh: 京，叔明之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Jing was the fifth-generation descendant of Shuming.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing was a fifth-generation descendant of Li Shuming.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以昭義節度副使、磁州刺史盧玄卿為洺州刺史兼魏博招討副使。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zhao-Yi deputy military commissioner and Cizhou prefect Lu Xuanqing was made Luozhou prefect and concurrently Wei-Bo campaign deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day Lu Xuanqing, deputy commissioner of Zhao-Yi and prefect of Ci, was made prefect of Luo and deputy commander of the campaign against Wei-Bo.

sentences.zh: 初，李抱真為澤潞節度使，馬燧領河陽三城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Baozhen was Ze-Lu military commissioner and Ma Sui held the three cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Baozhen had been military commissioner of Ze and Lu, while Ma Sui held the three Heyang cities.

sentences.zh: 抱真欲殺懷州刺史楊鉥，鉥奔燧。

translations.literal: Baozhen wished to kill Huaizhou prefect Yang Chu; Chu fled to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen meant to kill Yang Chu, prefect of Huai, and Chu fled to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧納之，且奏其無罪，抱真怒。

translations.literal: Sui accepted him and also memorialized that he was guiltless; Baozhen was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Sui sheltered him and memorialized that he was innocent. Baozhen was furious.

sentences.zh: 及同討田悅，數以事相恨望，二人怨隙遂深，不復相見。

translations.literal: When they campaigned together against Tian Yue, they repeatedly nursed grievances over affairs; the rift between the two deepened and they no longer met.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning together against Tian Yue, they nursed grievance after grievance until the breach between them was deep and they refused to meet.

sentences.zh: 由是諸軍逗橈，久無成功，上數遣中使和解之。

translations.literal: Because of this the various armies dallied and dragged; for long there was no success; the emperor repeatedly sent palace agents to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies stalled and victory eluded them for months, and the emperor repeatedly sent palace envoys to reconcile the two.

sentences.zh: 及王武俊逼趙州，抱真分麾下二千人戍邢州，燧大怒曰：「餘賊未除，宜相與戮力，乃分兵自守其地，我寧得獨戰邪！」

translations.literal: When Wang Wujun pressed Zhaozhou, Baozhen detached two thousand men from his command to garrison Xingzhou. Sui flew into a rage: "The remaining rebels are not yet destroyed—we should join forces, yet you divide troops to guard your own territory. Must I fight alone!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wujun pressed Zhaozhou, Baozhen detached two thousand men to hold Xing. Ma Sui raged: "The rebels are not beaten yet—we should fight as one, and you peel off troops to guard your own ground. Am I to fight alone?"

sentences.zh: 欲引兵歸。

translations.literal: He wished to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to pull his army out.

sentences.zh: 李晟說燧曰：「李尚書以邢、趙連壤，分兵守之，誠未有害。

translations.literal: Li Sheng persuaded Sui: "Minister Li, because Xing and Zhao share a border, divided troops to hold it—truly no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng urged him: "Minister Li posted men at Xing because it borders Zhao—that is no real injury to us.

sentences.zh: 今公遽自引去，眾謂公何！」

translations.literal: If you now abruptly withdraw on your own, what will the masses say of you!"
translations.idiomatic: If you march away now, what will the army say of you?"

sentences.zh: 燧悅，乃單騎造抱真壘，相與釋憾結歡。

translations.literal: Sui was pleased; he then rode alone to Baozhen's camp, and together they released resentments and renewed friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Sui took the counsel to heart, rode alone into Baozhen's camp, and the two cleared their grudges and made peace.

sentences.zh: 會洺州刺史田昂請入朝，燧奏以洺州隸抱真，請玄卿為刺史，兼充招討之副。

translations.literal: Just then Luozhou prefect Tian Ang requested to come to court; Sui memorialized that Luozhou be placed under Baozhen, asked that Xuanqing be prefect, and concurrently serve as campaign deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Ang, prefect of Luo, asked to come to court, Sui proposed placing Luo under Baozhen, with Xuanqing as prefect and deputy commander of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 李晟軍先隸抱真，又請兼隸燧，以示協和。

translations.literal: Li Sheng's army had first been under Baozhen; he also asked that it be placed under Sui as well, to show harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng's force had first served under Baozhen; he now asked that it answer to Sui as well, as a gesture of unity.

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度行軍司馬蔡廷玉惡判官鄭雲逵，言於朱泚，奏貶莫州參軍。

translations.literal: Lu-Long campaign adjutant Cai Tingyu hated registrar Zheng Yunkui and spoke to Zhu Ci, who memorialized demoting him to Mo prefecture aide.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tingyu, campaign adjutant of Lu-Long, hated the registrar Zheng Yunkui and persuaded Zhu Ci to have him demoted to a post in Mo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雲逵妻，朱滔之女也，滔復奏為掌書記。

translations.literal: Yunkui's wife was Zhu Tao's daughter; Tao again memorialized appointing him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yunkui's wife was Zhu Tao's daughter, and Tao had him restored as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 雲逵深構廷玉於滔，廷玉又與檢校大理少卿朱體微言於泚曰：「滔在幽鎮，事多專擅，其性非長者，不可以兵權付之。」

translations.literal: Yunkui deeply framed Tingyu with Tao; Tingyu also spoke with acting Grand Court Judge Zhu Tiwi to Ci: "Tao at You-zhou does many things on his own authority; his nature is not that of an elder—military authority must not be entrusted to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yunkui slandered Tingyu to Tao, while Tingyu and the acting Grand Court Judge Zhu Tiwi told Ci: "Tao runs You-zhou on his own whim. He is no steady elder—do not leave him the army."

sentences.zh: 滔知之，大怒，數與泚書，請殺二人者，泚不從。

translations.literal: Tao learned of this, grew greatly angry, and repeatedly wrote Ci asking to kill the two; Ci did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao learned of it he was furious and wrote Ci again and again demanding their deaths. Ci refused.

sentences.zh: 由是兄弟頗有隙。

translations.literal: From this the brothers had considerable friction.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the brothers were badly estranged.

sentences.zh: 及滔拒命，上欲歸罪於廷玉等以悅滔，甲子，貶廷玉柳州司戶，體微萬州南浦尉。

translations.literal: When Tao defied orders, the emperor wished to assign blame to Tingyu and others to please Tao; on jiazi, Tingyu was demoted to Lizhou registrar and Tiwi to Wanzhou Nanpu adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao defied the throne the emperor sought to appease him by punishing Tingyu and the rest. On jiazi, Tingyu was sent to Lizhou as registrar and Tiwi to Nanpu in Wanzhou as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使劉洽攻李納之濮陽，降其守將高彥昭。

translations.literal: Xuan-Wu commissioner Liu Qia attacked Li Na's Puyang and received the surrender of its defender Gao Yanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia of Xuan-Wu attacked Li Na's Puyang and won the surrender of its commander Gao Yanzhao.

sentences.zh: 朱滔遣人以蠟書置髻中遺朱泚，欲與同反。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao sent someone with a wax-sealed letter hidden in his hair knot to deliver to Zhu Ci, wishing to rebel together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao sent a man with a wax-sealed letter hidden in his topknot to Zhu Ci, urging a joint rebellion.

sentences.zh: 馬燧獲之，並使者送長安，泚不之知。

translations.literal: Ma Sui captured it and sent it with the messenger to Chang'an; Ci knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui seized the letter and the courier and sent both to Chang'an while Ci remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 上驛召泚於鳳翔，至，以蠟書並使者示之，泚惶恐頓首請罪。

translations.literal: By express post the emperor summoned Ci from Fengxiang; when he arrived, the wax letter and messenger were shown him; Ci in terror kowtowed and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Ci posthaste from Fengxiang. When he arrived the letter and courier were shown him, and Ci prostrated himself in terror to beg pardon.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「相去千里，初不同謀，非卿之罪也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A thousand li apart—you never plotted together at the start; this is not your fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You were a thousand li apart and never plotted together. This is not your fault."

sentences.zh: 因留之長安私第，賜名園、腴田、錦彩、金銀甚厚，以安其意；

translations.literal: He therefore kept him at a private residence in Chang'an and bestowed famous gardens, fertile fields, brocades, gold, and silver in great abundance to settle his mind;
translations.idiomatic: He kept Ci at a private house in Chang'an and heaped on him famous gardens, rich fields, brocades, gold, and silver to ease his mind;

sentences.zh: 其幽州、盧龍節度、太尉、中書令並如故。

translations.literal: his Youzhou and Lu-Long commissions, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Councilor all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: his posts in Youzhou and Lu-Long, his rank as Grand Preceptor, and his seat as Grand Councilor all remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 上以幽州兵在鳳翔，思得重臣代之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Youzhou troops were at Fengxiang, wished for a weighty minister to replace him there.
translations.idiomatic: With Youzhou troops still at Fengxiang, the emperor wanted a senior minister to take Ci's place there.

sentences.zh: 盧杞忌張鎰忠直，為上所重，欲出之於外，己得專總朝政，乃對曰：「朱泚名位素崇，鳳翔將校班秩已高，非宰相信臣，無以鎮撫，臣請自行。」

translations.literal: Lu Qi, who resented Zhang Yin's loyal uprightness and that the emperor valued him, wished to send him outward so that he himself might monopolize court government, answered: "Zhu Ci's name and rank have always been lofty; Fengxiang's officers already hold high grades—none but a chief minister or trusted minister can pacify them. Your servant asks to go in person."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi resented Zhang Yin's upright loyalty and the favor the emperor showed him. Qi wanted Yin sent away so he could rule the court alone. He answered: "Zhu Ci's standing is too high and Fengxiang's officers too senior—only a chief minister or trusted minister can hold them. I beg to go myself."

sentences.zh: 上俯首未言，□巳又曰：「陛下必以臣貌寢，不為三軍所伏，固惟陛下神算。」

translations.literal: The emperor bowed his head and did not speak; Lu Qi said again: "If Your Majesty surely thinks my appearance is unimposing and the three armies will not submit to me, that rests entirely with Your Majesty's divine calculation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed his head in silence. Lu Qi added: "If Your Majesty thinks my looks too slight for the troops to respect, that is for Your Majesty's wisdom alone to decide."

sentences.zh: 上乃顧鎰曰：「才兼文武，望重內外，無以易卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor then turned to Yin: "Talent spanning civil and military, esteem heavy within and without—none can replace you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Yin and said: "Civil and military talent, renown at court and in the field—no one can take your place."

sentences.zh: 鎰知為杞所排而無辭以免，因再拜受命。

translations.literal: Yin knew he had been pushed aside by Qi and had no words to refuse; he twice bowed and accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yin knew Qi had maneuvered him out and had no excuse to refuse. He bowed twice and accepted.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以鎰兼鳳翔尹、隴右節度等使。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Yin was made concurrently Fengxiang prefect, Longyou commissioner, and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day Yin was appointed concurrently prefect of Fengxiang, commissioner of Longyou, and related commands.

sentences.zh: 初，盧杞與御史大夫嚴郢共構楊炎、趙惠伯之獄，炎死，杞復忌郢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Qi and censor-in-chief Yan Yan together framed the cases of Yang Yan and Zhao Huibo; after Yang Yan died, Qi again resented Yan Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lu Qi and the censor-in-chief Yan Yan had together framed Yang Yan and Zhao Huibo. After Yang Yan died, Qi came to resent Yan Yan as well.

sentences.zh: 會蔡廷玉等貶官，殿中侍御史鄭詹誤遞文符至昭應送之，廷玉等行已至藍田，召還而東，廷玉等以為執己送朱滔，至靈寶西，赴河死。

translations.literal: It happened that Cai Tingyu and others were demoted officials; Palace Attendant Censor Zheng Zhan mistakenly forwarded the document tally to Zhaoying to escort them; Tingyu and company had already reached Lantian when recalled and sent east; they thought they were being seized and sent to Zhu Tao; west of Lingbao they threw themselves into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Cai Tingyu and other demoted officials were in transit. Palace Attendant Censor Zheng Zhan mistakenly routed the escort papers to Zhaoying. Tingyu's party had already reached Lantian when they were recalled and ordered east. Believing they were being seized and handed over to Zhu Tao, they drowned themselves in the river west of Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，駭異，盧杞因奏：「朱泚必疑以為詔旨，請遣三司使案詹。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and was shocked and alarmed; Lu Qi thereupon memorialized: "Zhu Ci will surely suspect this was an imperial edict—please send the Three Agencies commissioner to investigate Zhan."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he was appalled. Lu Qi thereupon memorialized: "Zhu Ci is sure to suspect this was an imperial order. Please send a Three Agencies commissioner to investigate Zhan."

sentences.zh: 又言：「御史所為，必稟大夫，請並郢案之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "What a censor does must surely be reported to the chief censor—please investigate Yan as well."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Whatever a censor does, the chief censor must have been told. Please investigate Yan Yan as well."

sentences.zh: 獄未具，壬午，杞奏杖殺詹於京兆府；

translations.literal: Before the case was complete, on renwu Qi memorialized to have Zhan beaten to death at the Jingzhao prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Before the trial was finished, on the renwu day Qi memorialized to have Zhan beaten to death in the Jingzhao prefecture office;

sentences.zh: 貶郢費州刺史，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: Yan Yan was demoted to prefect of Feizhou and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yan was demoted to prefect of Feizhou and died on the way to exile.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，崔祐甫為相，務崇寬大，故當時政聲藹然，以為有貞觀之風。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, Cui Youfu was chancellor and devoted himself to magnanimity, so the government's reputation at the time was harmonious and people thought there was a Zhenguan-era air.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first ascended the throne, Cui Youfu served as chancellor and pursued a policy of leniency. Government at the time won a glowing reputation; many thought the Zhenguan spirit had returned.

sentences.zh: 及盧杞為相，知上性多忌，因以疑似離間群臣，始勸上以嚴刻御下，中外失望。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi became chancellor, knowing the emperor's nature was much given to suspicion, he used supposed doubts to estrange the ministers, and began urging the emperor to govern subordinates with severity; court and countryside alike were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lu Qi became chancellor, knowing how suspicious the emperor was, he sowed doubt among the ministers and began urging harsh rule. Court and country alike lost hope.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少游奏，本道稅錢每千請增二百。

translations.literal: Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou memorialized that in his circuit taxes per thousand cash should be increased by two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou memorialized that taxes in his circuit should rise by two hundred cash per thousand collected.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙戌，詔增它道稅錢皆如淮南；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingxu, an edict ordered that tax increases in every other circuit should match Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingxu day, an edict ordered every other circuit to raise taxes to match Huainan;

sentences.zh: 又鹽每斗價皆增百錢。

translations.literal: salt too was increased by a hundred cash per dou in price.
translations.idiomatic: and the price of salt was raised by a hundred cash per dou everywhere as well.

sentences.zh: 朱滔、王武俊自寧晉南救魏州，辛卯，詔朔方節度使李懷光將朔方及神策步騎萬五千人東討田悅，且拒滔等。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun marched south from Ningjin to rescue Weizhou; on xinmao an edict ordered Shuofang commissioner Li Huaiguang to lead fifteen thousand Shuofang and Shence infantry and cavalry east to attack Tian Yue and also to block Tao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun marched south from Ningjin to relieve Weizhou. On the xinmao day an edict ordered Shuofang commissioner Li Huaiguang to lead fifteen thousand Shuofang and Shence foot and horse east against Tian Yue and to hold off Tao and his allies.

sentences.zh: 滔行至宗城，掌書記鄭雲逵、參謀田景仙棄滔來降。

translations.literal: When Tao reached Zongcheng, registrar Zheng Yunkui and staff adviser Tian Jingxian abandoned Tao and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao reached Zongcheng, his registrar Zheng Yunkui and staff adviser Tian Jingxian deserted him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，加河東節度使馬燧同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingyou Ma Sui, commissioner of Hedong, was given the additional title of Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day Ma Sui, commissioner of Hedong, was made a chief minister as well.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，置義武軍節度於定州，以易、定、滄三州隸之。

translations.literal: On xinhai the Yiwu Army command was established at Dingzhou, with Yi, Ding, and Cang prefectures placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day the Yiwu Army command was established at Dingzhou, with Yi, Ding, and Cang prefectures placed under it.

sentences.zh: 張光晟之殺突董也，上欲遂絕回紇，召冊可汗使源休還太原。

translations.literal: When Zhang Guangcheng killed Tudun, the emperor wished to break with the Uyghurs entirely and recalled enfeoffment envoy Yuan Xiu to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Guangcheng killed Tudun, the emperor wanted to cut ties with the Uyghurs altogether and recalled enfeoffment envoy Yuan Xiu to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃復遣休送突董及翳密施、大、小梅錄等四喪還其國，可汗遣其宰相頡子思迦等迎之。

translations.literal: After a long while he again sent Xiu to escort back the four coffins of Tudun and Yimishi, Da Mei, and Xiao Mei Lu and others to their country; the qaghan sent his chancellor Ezesik and others to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: After a long delay he again sent Xiu to return the four coffins—Tudun, Yimishi, Da Mei, and Xiao Mei Lu—to the Uyghur realm. The qaghan sent his chancellor Ezesik and others to meet them.

sentences.zh: 頡子思迦坐大帳，立休等於帳前雪中，詰以殺突董之狀，欲殺者數四，供待甚薄。

translations.literal: Ezesik sat in a great tent and had Xiu and the others stand in the snow before the tent, questioning them about the killing of Tudun; several times he was on the verge of killing them, and provisions were very scant.
translations.idiomatic: Ezesik sat in a great tent and made Xiu and his party stand in the snow outside, interrogating them about Tudun's death. Several times he nearly had them killed, and their rations were miserably thin.

sentences.zh: 留五十餘日，乃得歸。

translations.literal: They were detained more than fifty days before they could return.
translations.idiomatic: They were held more than fifty days before they were allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 可汗使人謂之曰：「國人皆欲殺汝以償怨，我意則不然。

translations.literal: The qaghan sent someone to tell them: "Our people all wish to kill you to repay the grievance; my own mind is otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan sent word: "My people all want to kill you to settle the score. I do not agree.

sentences.zh: 汝國已殺突董等，我又殺汝，如以血洗血，污益甚耳！

translations.literal: Your state has already killed Tudun and the others; if I kill you too, it is like washing blood with blood—the stain only grows worse!
translations.idiomatic: Your country has already killed Tudun and the rest. If I kill you as well, that is washing blood with blood—the stain only deepens!

sentences.zh: 今吾以水洗血，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: Now if I wash the blood with water, is that not better!
translations.idiomatic: Better to wash the blood away with water—is that not wiser?

sentences.zh: 唐負我馬直絹百八十萬匹，當速歸之。」

translations.literal: Tang still owes me one million eight hundred thousand bolts of silk for horse payments—you should return them quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Tang still owes me one million eight hundred thousand bolts of silk for our horses. Return them at once."

sentences.zh: 遣其散支將軍康赤心隨休入見，休竟不得見可汗而還。

translations.literal: He sent his Sanzhi general Kang Chixin to accompany Xiu to an audience; Xiu in the end did not obtain an audience with the qaghan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his Sanzhi general Kang Chixin to accompany Xiu to court. Xiu never obtained an audience with the qaghan and turned back.

sentences.zh: 六月，己卯，至長安，詔以帛十萬匹、金銀十萬兩償其馬直。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jimao, he reached Chang'an; an edict ordered a hundred thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand taels of gold and silver to repay the horse payments.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jimao day, he reached Chang'an. An edict ordered a hundred thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand taels of gold and silver sent as payment for the horses.

sentences.zh: 休有口辯，盧杞恐其見上得幸，乘其未至，先除光祿卿。

translations.literal: Xiu was eloquent; Lu Qi feared that if he saw the emperor he would win favor, and before Xiu arrived had him appointed Guanglu Director first.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was a gifted speaker. Lu Qi feared he would win the emperor's favor if he appeared at court, and before Xiu arrived had him appointed Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 朱滔、王武俊軍至魏州，田悅具牛酒出迎，魏人歡呼動地。

translations.literal: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun's armies reached Weizhou, Tian Yue furnished oxen and wine to go out and welcome them; the people of Wei shouted until the ground shook.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun's armies reached Weizhou, Tian Yue went out with oxen and wine to welcome them. The people of Wei cheered until the earth seemed to tremble.

sentences.zh: 滔營於愜山，是日，李懷光軍亦至，馬燧等盛軍容迎之。

translations.literal: Tao camped at Qieshan; that day Li Huaiguang's army also arrived, and Ma Sui and others displayed full military array to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao encamped at Qieshan. That same day Li Huaiguang's army arrived, and Ma Sui and the others turned out their full strength in ceremony to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 滔以為襲己，遽出陳。

translations.literal: Tao thought they were attacking him and rushed out to form battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Tao thought he was under attack and rushed his men into battle formation.

sentences.zh: 懷光勇而無謀，欲乘其營壘未就擊之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was brave but lacked strategy and wished to strike while their ramparts were not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was brave but rash. He wanted to strike before the rebels' camp was fully built.

sentences.zh: 燧請且休將士，觀釁而動，懷光曰：「彼營壘既立，將為後患，此時不可失也。」

translations.literal: Sui asked to rest the troops first and watch for an opening; Huaiguang said, "Once their ramparts are set up they will become a later trouble—this moment cannot be missed."
translations.idiomatic: Sui urged resting the men and waiting for an opening. Huaiguang said, "Once their ramparts stand they will plague us later. We cannot miss this chance."

sentences.zh: 遂擊滔於愜山之西，殺步卒千餘人，滔軍崩沮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked Tao west of Qieshan, killing more than a thousand foot soldiers; Tao's army collapsed in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Tao west of Qieshan, killing more than a thousand foot soldiers. Tao's army broke and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 懷光按轡觀之，有喜色。

translations.literal: Huaiguang held his reins and watched, with a look of pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang reined in his horse to watch, his face bright with satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 士卒爭入滔營取寶貨，王武俊引二千騎橫衝懷光軍，軍分為二。

translations.literal: Soldiers scrambled into Tao's camp to seize treasure; Wang Wujun led two thousand horsemen in a lateral charge through Huaiguang's army and split it in two.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers rushed into Tao's camp to loot. Wang Wujun led two thousand horsemen in a flanking charge through Huaiguang's ranks and cut his army in half.

sentences.zh: 滔引後繼之，官軍大敗，蹙入永濟渠溺死者不可勝數，人相蹈藉，其積如山，水為之不流，馬燧等各收軍保壘。

translations.literal: Tao brought up the rear to press on; the imperial army was utterly defeated, driven into the Yongji Canal where the drowned were beyond counting—men trampled one another until the piles were like hills and the water would not flow; Ma Sui and the others each withdrew their armies to their ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao brought up reinforcements and pressed the attack. The imperial army was routed and driven into the Yongji Canal; the drowned were beyond count. Men trampled one another until the bodies piled like hills and the water stopped moving. Ma Sui and the others each pulled their forces back behind their walls.

sentences.zh: 是夕，滔等堰永濟渠入王莽故河，絕官軍糧道及歸路。

translations.literal: That night Tao and the others dammed the Yongji Canal into the old Wang Mang river course, cutting the imperial army's grain route and line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tao and his allies dammed the Yongji Canal into Wang Mang's old channel, severing the imperial army's supply line and retreat.

sentences.zh: 明日，水深三尺餘。

translations.literal: The next day the water was more than three chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: By the next day the water stood more than three chi deep.

sentences.zh: 馬燧懼，遣使卑辭謝滔，求與諸節度歸本道，奏天子，請以河北事委五郎處之。

translations.literal: Ma Sui was afraid and sent an envoy with humble words to apologize to Tao, asking that the various commissioners return to their own circuits and report to the Son of Heaven, requesting that affairs north of the Yellow River be entrusted to the Fifth Lord's handling.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui was terrified. He sent an envoy with abject apologies to Tao, asking that all the commissioners be allowed to return to their circuits and report to the throne, and offering to leave affairs north of the Yellow River entirely to the Fifth Lord's discretion.

sentences.zh: 滔欲許之，王武俊以為不可。

translations.literal: Tao wished to agree; Wang Wujun said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was inclined to accept. Wang Wujun said he must not.

sentences.zh: 滔不從。

translations.literal: Tao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tao would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，燧與諸軍涉水而西，退保魏縣以拒滔，滔乃謝武俊，武俊由是恨滔。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Sui and the various armies waded west through the water, falling back to guard Weixian to resist Tao; Tao then apologized to Wujun, and Wujun came to resent Tao because of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Sui and the allied armies waded west through the flood and fell back to Weixian to hold off Tao. Tao then apologized to Wujun, who from that day bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 後數日，滔等亦引兵營魏縣東南，與官軍隔水相拒。

translations.literal: Several days later Tao and the others also withdrew their armies to camp southeast of Weixian, facing the imperial army across the water in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Tao and his allies also withdrew to camp southeast of Weixian, facing the imperial army across the water in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 李納求援於滔等，滔遣魏博兵馬使信都承慶將兵助之。

translations.literal: Li Na sought aid from Tao and the others; Tao sent Weibo army-and-horse commissioner Xindu Chengqing with troops to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na asked Tao and the others for help. Tao sent Weibo army-and-horse commissioner Xindu Chengqing with troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 納攻宋州，不克，遣兵馬使李克信、李欽遙戍濮陽、南華以拒劉洽。

translations.literal: Na attacked Songzhou but could not take it; he sent army-and-horse commissioners Li Kexin and Li Qinyao to garrison Puyang and Nanhua to resist Liu Qia.
translations.idiomatic: Na attacked Songzhou but failed to take it. He sent army-and-horse commissioners Li Kexin and Li Qinyao to hold Puyang and Nanhua against Liu Qia.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以淮寧節度使李希烈兼平盧、淄青、兗鄆、登萊、齊州節度使，討李納。

translations.literal: On jiachen Li Xilie, pacification commissioner of Huaining, was made concurrently commissioner of Pinglu, Ziqing, Yanzhou-Jizhou, Dengzhou-Laizhou, and Qizhou to attack Li Na.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day Li Xilie, pacification commissioner of Huaining, was made concurrently commissioner of Pinglu, Ziqing, Yan-Ji, Deng-Lai, and Qi to campaign against Li Na.

sentences.zh: 又以河東節度使馬燧兼魏博、澶相節度使。

translations.literal: Ma Sui, commissioner of Hedong, was also made concurrently commissioner of Weibo and Cao-Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui, commissioner of Hedong, was also made concurrently commissioner of Weibo and Cao-Xiang.

sentences.zh: 加朔方、邠寧節度使李懷光同平章事。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang, commissioner of Shuofang and Bin-Ning, was given the additional title of Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang, commissioner of Shuofang and Bin-Ning, was made a chief minister as well.

sentences.zh: 神策行營招討使李晟請以所將兵北解趙州之圍，與張孝忠合勢圖范陽，上許之，晟自魏州引兵北趨趙州，王士真解圍去。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Li Sheng of the Shence mobile camp asked to lead his troops north to relieve the siege of Zhaozhou and join forces with Zhang Xiaozhong to plot against Fanyang; the emperor assented; Sheng led his army north from Weizhou toward Zhaozhou, and Wang Shizhen lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng, pacification commissioner of the Shence mobile camp, asked to march north with his troops to lift the siege of Zhaozhou and join Zhang Xiaozhong against Fanyang. The emperor agreed. Sheng led his army north from Weizhou toward Zhaozhou, and Wang Shizhen broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晟留趙州三日，與孝忠合兵北略恆州。

translations.literal: Sheng remained at Zhaozhou three days, then united with Xiaozhong's army and marched north to threaten Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng stayed at Zhaozhou three days, then united with Xiaozhong and marched north to threaten Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 演州司馬李孟秋舉兵反，自稱安南節度使。

translations.literal: Yanzhou acting prefect Li Mengqiu raised troops in revolt and styled himself commissioner of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou acting prefect Li Mengqiu raised troops in rebellion and styled himself military commissioner of Annan.

sentences.zh: 安南都護輔良交討斬之。

translations.literal: Annan protector Fu Liangjiao attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Annan protector Fu Liangjiao campaigned against him and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁未，置汴東、西水陸運、兩稅、鹽鐵使二人，度支總其大要而已。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingwei, two commissioners for Bian east and west water-and-land transport, the two taxes, and salt and iron were appointed—the Ministry of Revenue would oversee the general outline only.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dingwei day, two commissioners were appointed for Bian east and west water-and-land transport, the two taxes, and salt and iron; the Ministry of Revenue would retain only overall supervision.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以涇原留後姚令言為節度使。

translations.literal: On xinyou Yao Lingyan, acting commissioner of Jingyuan, was made full commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day Yao Lingyan, acting commissioner of Jingyuan, was made full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 盧杞惡太子太師顏真卿，欲出之於外。

translations.literal: Lu Qi hated Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yan Zhenqing and wished to send him outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi hated Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yan Zhenqing and wanted to post him outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 真卿謂杞曰：「先中丞傳首至平原，真卿以舌舐面血。

translations.literal: Zhenqing said to Qi, "When the late Central Grand Secretary's head reached Pingyuan, Zhenqing licked the blood on his face with my tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing told Qi, "When my late brother's severed head reached Pingyuan, I licked the blood from his face with my own tongue.

sentences.zh: 今相公忍不相容乎！」

translations.literal: Will the Chancellor now bear not to tolerate me!"
translations.idiomatic: Can the Chancellor truly bear not to make room for me now!"

sentences.zh: 杞矍然起拜，然恨之益甚。

translations.literal: Qi started up and bowed in alarm, yet hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Qi started up and bowed in alarm, yet hated him all the more deeply.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸卯，殿中少監崔漢衡自吐蕃歸，贊普遣其臣區頰贊隨漢衡入見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guimao, Palace Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Hanheng returned from Tibet; the tsenpo sent his minister Qupozhan to accompany Hanheng to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the guimao day, Palace Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Hanheng returned from Tibet. The tsenpo sent his minister Qupozhan to accompany Hanheng to court.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，以湖南觀察使曹王皋為江南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinhai Cao Wang Gao, observer of Hunan, was made commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinhai day, Cao Wang Gao, observer of Hunan, was made military commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 皋至洪州，悉集將佐，簡閱其才，得牙將伊慎、王鍔等，擢為大將，引荊襄判官許孟容置幕府。

translations.literal: When Gao reached Hongzhou he gathered all generals and staff, sifted their talents, obtained military adjutants Yi Shen and Wang E and others and promoted them to great generals, and brought Jing-Xiang judge Xu Mengrong into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao reached Hongzhou he gathered every officer and aide, sifted their abilities, found military adjutants Yi Shen and Wang E among others and promoted them to senior commanders, and brought Jing-Xiang judge Xu Mengrong onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 慎，兗州人；

translations.literal: Shen was a man of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Shen was from Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 孟容，長安人也。

translations.literal: Mengrong was a man of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong was from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 慎常從李希烈討梁崇義，希烈愛其才，欲留之，慎逃歸。

translations.literal: Shen had often followed Li Xilie against Liang Chongyi; Xilie admired his talent and wished to keep him, but Shen fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had often campaigned under Li Xilie against Liang Chongyi. Xilie admired his ability and wanted to keep him, but Shen escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 希烈聞皋用慎，恐為己患，遺慎七屬甲，詐為復書，墜之境上。

translations.literal: When Xilie heard Gao was employing Shen, fearing he would become a threat, he sent Shen seven-layer armor, forging a reply letter, and dropped it inside the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie heard Gao had taken Shen into service, fearing a future threat he sent Shen a suit of seven-layer armor with a forged letter of reply and had it dropped inside the border.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣中使即軍中斬慎，皋為之論雪；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sent a palace envoy to the army at once to execute Shen; Gao pleaded his innocence for him;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he sent a palace envoy to the army to execute Shen on the spot. Gao pleaded his case;

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: there was no reply yet.
translations.idiomatic: but no answer came.

sentences.zh: 會江賊三千餘眾入寇，皋遣慎擊賊自贖；

translations.literal: When over three thousand river bandits invaded, Gao sent Shen to strike the bandits and redeem himself;
translations.idiomatic: Just then more than three thousand river pirates raided the district. Gao sent Shen against them to win his life back;

sentences.zh: 慎擊破之，斬首數百級而還，由是得免。

translations.literal: Shen broke them, returned after beheading several hundred heads, and thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shen routed them, returned with several hundred heads, and was spared.

sentences.zh: 盧杞秉政，知上必更立相，恐其分己權，乘間薦吏部侍郎關播儒厚，可以鎮風俗。

translations.literal: Lu Qi held power and knew the emperor would surely appoint another chancellor; fearing his authority would be divided, he seized an opportunity to recommend Vice Minister of Personnel Guan Bo as cultured and generous—able to settle custom.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi held the reins of government and knew the emperor would soon name another chancellor. Fearful of sharing power, he seized a chance to recommend Vice Minister of Personnel Guan Bo as a cultured, steady man who could steady public morals.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以播為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingchen Bo was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day Bo was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 政事皆決於杞，播等斂衽無所可否。

translations.literal: Government affairs were all decided by Qi; Bo and the others drew in their robes and had nothing to affirm or deny.
translations.idiomatic: All government business was decided by Qi. Bo and the others sat with hands folded and never assented or objected.

sentences.zh: 上嘗從容與宰相論事，播意有所不可，起立欲言，杞目之而止。

translations.literal: Once the emperor discussed affairs at ease with the chancellors; Bo inwardly disapproved but rose intending to speak; Qi glanced at him and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor discussed policy at ease with his chancellors. Bo disagreed inwardly, rose to speak, and Qi shot him a look that silenced him.

sentences.zh: 還至中書，杞謂播曰：「以足下端愨少言，故相引至此，曏者奈何發口欲言邪！」

translations.literal: Returning to the Secretariat, Qi said to Bo, "Because you, sir, are upright and sparing of speech, I therefore drew you here—just now why did you open your mouth intending to speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Back at the Secretariat, Qi told Bo, "I brought you here because you are upright and keep quiet. Why did you just now open your mouth to speak!"

sentences.zh: 播自是不復敢言。

translations.literal: From then on Bo never again dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Bo never dared speak again.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，遣都官員外郎河中樊澤使於吐蕃，告以結盟之期。

translations.literal: On wuchen the Director of Court Ceremonies Fan Ze of Hexia was sent as envoy to Tibet to announce the date of the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day Fan Ze of Hexia, Director of Court Ceremonies, was sent as envoy to Tibet to announce the date set for the alliance.

sentences.zh: 丙子，肅王詳薨。

translations.literal: On bingzi Prince Su Xiang died.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day Prince Su Xiang died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯朔，加淮南節度使陳少游同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jimao the first of the month, Huainan commissioner Chen Shaoyou was given the additional title of Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day jimao, Huainan commissioner Chen Shaoyou was made a chief minister as well.

sentences.zh: 田悅德朱滔之救，與王武俊議奉滔為主，稱臣事之，滔不可，曰：「愜山之捷，皆大夫二兄之力，滔何敢獨居尊位！」

translations.literal: Tian Yue was grateful for Zhu Tao's rescue and discussed with Wang Wujun making Tao their lord and serving him as subject with ministerial rites; Tao refused, saying, "The victory at Qieshan was entirely through the two elder brothers the Great Physician's strength—how could Tao alone occupy the highest position!"
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Zhu Tao's rescue, Tian Yue discussed with Wang Wujun making Tao their sovereign and serving him as vassals. Tao refused, saying, "The victory at Qieshan was won by you two elder brothers, Great Physicians—how could I alone take the highest seat!"

sentences.zh: 於是幽州判官李子千、恆冀判官鄭濡等共議：「請與鄆州李大夫為四國，俱稱王而不改年號，如昔諸侯奉周家正朔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Youzhou judge Li Ziqian, Heng-Ji judge Zheng Ru, and others jointly proposed: "Let us together with Yanzhou's Lord Li be four kingdoms, each styling himself king without changing the reign era, as in the past when feudal lords observed the Zhou orthodox calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Youzhou judge Li Ziqian, Heng-Ji judge Zheng Ru, and others jointly proposed: "Let us join Yanzhou's Lord Li as four kingdoms, each take the title of king without changing the reign era, as feudal lords once did under the Zhou calendar.

sentences.zh: 築壇同盟，有不如約者，眾共伐之。

translations.literal: Let us build an altar and swear alliance: whoever fails the covenant, all will attack him together.
translations.idiomatic: Let us build an altar and swear alliance: whoever breaks the pact, all the rest shall attack him together.

sentences.zh: 不然，豈得常為叛臣，茫然無主，用兵既無名，有功無官爵為賞，使將吏何所依歸乎！」

translations.literal: Otherwise how can we forever be rebellious subjects with no lord, waging war without a name—when there is merit there is no official rank as reward; what can officers and clerks rely on!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we remain rebels without a lord forever, fighting wars without a proper name, winning battles with no ranks or rewards to give—what can our officers and clerks look to for their future!"

sentences.zh: 滔等皆以為然。

translations.literal: Tao and the others all thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and the others all agreed.

sentences.zh: 滔乃自稱冀王，田悅稱魏王，王武俊稱趙王，仍請李納稱齊王。

translations.literal: Tao then styled himself King of Ji, Tian Yue King of Wei, Wang Wujun King of Zhao, and still asked Li Na to style himself King of Qi.
