translations.idiomatic: Tao styled himself King of Ji, Tian Yue King of Wei, Wang Wujun King of Zhao, and asked Li Na to take the title King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 是日，滔等築壇於軍中，告天而受之。

translations.literal: That day Tao and the others built an altar in the army, reported to Heaven, and received the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: That day they built an altar in camp, reported to Heaven, and received their investiture.

sentences.zh: 滔為盟主，稱孤；

translations.literal: Tao as covenant lord called himself "I";
translations.idiomatic: As covenant lord Tao used the royal "I";

sentences.zh: 武俊、悅、納稱寡人。

translations.literal: Wujun, Yue, and Na called themselves "This unworthy one."
translations.idiomatic: Wujun, Yue, and Na used the humbler "this unworthy one."

sentences.zh: 所居堂曰殿，處分曰令，群下上書曰箋，妻曰妃，長子曰世子。

translations.literal: The hall where they dwelt was called a palace; decisions were called orders; subordinates' memorials were called memorials; wives were called consorts; eldest sons were called heirs apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Their halls were called palaces, their orders called commands, subordinates' reports called memorials, their wives consorts, and their eldest sons heirs apparent.

sentences.zh: 各以其所治州為府，置留守兼元帥，以軍政委之；

translations.literal: Each made his governing prefecture a "prefecture" and appointed resident deputies concurrently as marshals, entrusting military affairs to them;
translations.idiomatic: Each made his governing prefecture a capital "prefecture," appointed resident deputies who were also marshals, and entrusted military affairs to them;

sentences.zh: 又置東西曹，視門下、中書省；

translations.literal: they also set east and west bureaus, modeled on the Gate Department and Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: they also set east and west bureaus modeled on the Gate Department and Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 左右內史，視侍中、中書令；

translations.literal: left and right inner secretaries, modeled on Attendant-in-chief and Secretariat Director;
translations.idiomatic: left and right inner secretaries modeled on Attendant-in-chief and Secretariat Director;

sentences.zh: 餘官皆仿天朝而易其名。

translations.literal: all other offices imitated the imperial court but with changed names.
translations.idiomatic: all other offices copied the imperial court but under new names.

sentences.zh: 武俊以孟華為司禮尚書，華竟不受，嘔血死。

translations.literal: Wujun made Meng Hua Minister of Rites; Hua ultimately would not accept and died vomiting blood.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun appointed Meng Hua Minister of Rites. Hua refused to serve and died vomiting blood.

sentences.zh: 以兵馬使衛常寧為內史監，委以軍事。

translations.literal: He made army-and-horse commissioner Wei Changning Director of the Inner Secretariat and entrusted military affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: He made army-and-horse commissioner Wei Changning Director of the Inner Secretariat and entrusted him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 常寧謀殺武俊，武俊腰斬之。

translations.literal: Changning plotted to kill Wujun; Wujun cut him in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Changning plotted to assassinate Wujun. Wujun had him cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 武俊遣其將張終葵寇趙州，康日知擊斬之。

translations.literal: Wujun sent his general Zhang Zhongkui to raid Zhaozhou; Kang Rizhi attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun sent his general Zhang Zhongkui to raid Zhaozhou. Kang Rizhi struck back and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 李希烈帥所部兵三萬徙鎮許州，遣所親詣李納，與謀共襲汴州。

translations.literal: Li Xilie led his own troops, thirty thousand, to transfer his garrison to Xuzhou and sent a close associate to Li Na to plot jointly attacking Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie led thirty thousand of his own troops to transfer his command to Xuzhou and sent a close associate to Li Na to plot a joint strike on Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣使告李勉，云已兼領淄青，欲假道之官。

translations.literal: He sent envoys telling Li Mian that he had been made concurrently commissioner of Ziqing and wished to borrow the route to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Li Mian saying he had been made commissioner of Ziqing as well and wished to pass through on his way to take office.

sentences.zh: 勉為之治橋、具饌以待之，而嚴為之備。

translations.literal: Mian built bridges and prepared provisions to welcome him, yet strictly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Mian built bridges and laid out a feast to welcome him, but also made strict defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 希烈竟不至，又密與朱滔等交通，納亦數遣遊兵渡汴以迎希烈。

translations.literal: Xilie in the end did not come; he also secretly communicated with Zhu Tao and the others, and Na too repeatedly sent roving troops across the Bian to welcome Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie never came. He also communicated secretly with Zhu Tao and the others, and Na repeatedly sent roving troops across the Bian River to meet him.

sentences.zh: 由是東南轉輸者皆不敢由汴渠，自蔡水而上。

translations.literal: Because of this those transporting supplies southeast dared not use the Bian canal and went up by the Cai River instead.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this supply convoys from the southeast dared not use the Bian Canal and went up the Cai River instead.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁丑，李希烈自稱天下都元帥、太尉、建興王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, Li Xilie styled himself Supreme Commander of All Under Heaven, Grand Marshal, and King of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the dingchou day, Li Xilie styled himself Supreme Commander of All Under Heaven, Grand Marshal, and King of Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 時朱滔等與官軍相拒累月，官軍有度支饋糧，諸道益兵，而滔與王武俊孤軍深入，專仰給於田悅，客主日益困弊。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao and the others had faced the government army for many months; the government forces received grain from the Revenue Commission and reinforcements from the circuits, while Tao and Wang Wujun, a lone army deep in enemy country, relied solely on Tian Yue for supplies—host and guest grew daily more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao and his allies had been locked with the imperial armies for months; the court fed its troops through the Revenue Commission and poured in reinforcements from every circuit, while Tao and Wang Wujun, cut off deep in hostile territory, depended entirely on Tian Yue for supplies—both sides wore thinner by the day.

sentences.zh: 聞李希烈軍勢甚盛，頗怨望，乃相與謀遣使詣許州，勸希烈稱帝，希烈由是自稱天下都元帥。

translations.literal: Hearing that Li Xilie's army was very strong, they grew resentful and together plotted to send envoys to Xuzhou to urge Xilie to declare himself emperor; Xilie thereby styled himself Chief Commander of All under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard how powerful Li Xilie's forces had become, resentment turned to conspiracy: they would send envoys to Xuzhou to urge him to take the throne—and Xilie thereupon proclaimed himself supreme commander of all the realm.

sentences.zh: 司天少監徐承嗣請更造《建中正元曆》；

translations.literal: Xu Chengsi, vice director of the Directorate of Astronomy, requested that a new Jianzhong Zhengyuan calendar be compiled;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chengsi, vice director of the Directorate of Astronomy, petitioned to compile a new Jianzhong-Zhengyuan calendar;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor approved.
